Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-chatgpt

# Use your ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription in Claude Code

Claude Code can run on the GPT models of your ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan. Sign in to ChatGPT in magpie, pick a `codex/…` model for Claude Code, and keep working as before. No OpenAI API key.

Claude Code speaks Anthropic’s Messages API. magpie runs a gateway on your computer, at `127.0.0.1:3425`, that translates each of Claude Code’s requests for the GPT model and each reply back, streaming and tool calls included. magpie writes the gateway’s address and key into Claude Code’s `settings.json`, and your ChatGPT sign-in stays in magpie.

## Sign in to ChatGPT

1. **Open Add provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider.
2. **Click the ChatGPT tile.** magpie opens OpenAI’s own sign-in page in your browser. The account shows up as soon as you finish.

Or from a terminal:

```
magpie accounts add codex      # sign in to a ChatGPT account
```

The account’s models are `codex/…`.

## Pick a GPT model for Claude Code

In the Agents tab, click the model on Claude Code’s row and choose a `codex/…` model. From a terminal:

```
magpie models                  # every model, as provider/model
magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5
```

Inside Claude Code, `/model` lists magpie’s models too, marked “via magpie”, so you can switch there.

> **Only some sessions on GPT?** Leave Claude Code unconnected in magpie and run `claude-magpie` when you want it on a GPT model. It starts the same `claude` with magpie’s settings for that session only, and `settings.json` is not rewritten.

## How Opus, Sonnet and Haiku map

Claude Code asks for models by tier: `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` and `fable`. Its own small jobs, such as a session’s title and Explore subagents, go to the haiku tier. With a GPT model as the main model:

| Tier | Variable in `env` | By default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| opus | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` | The GPT model you picked |
| sonnet | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` | The GPT model you picked |
| haiku | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` | The GPT model you picked |
| fable | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` | Left unset |

To give a tier a model of its own, say a smaller one for haiku, set it on Claude Code’s row in magpie, or from a terminal:

```
magpie claude haiku codex/…    # one tier on its own model
magpie claude haiku ""         # back to the main model
```

## Reasoning effort

The effort Claude Code asks for goes to the GPT model as its reasoning effort, on requests where Claude Code has thinking on. magpie also tells Claude Code which effort levels each model has.

To hold one effort whatever Claude Code asks, set effort on Claude Code’s row. opus effort, sonnet effort, haiku effort, fable effort and subagent effort set it per tier. Each starts at the effort Claude Code asks for. An open Claude Code session keeps the effort it started with, so restart it to use a new one.

## Limits and usage

Requests are served on your ChatGPT account, so they count toward your plan’s usage limits, as Codex’s own requests do.

- **See what’s used..** Turn on status line on Claude Code’s row: it shows the 5h and 7d use of the accounts magpie serves, under Claude Code’s prompt. `magpie accounts` lists each account and how much of its allowance is used. The Usage tab has the history.
- **When an account runs out..** magpie sets it aside until the reset OpenAI’s refusal names, else until its full window renews, else for 5 hours, and sends requests to your next account or the provider’s Fallback. The account comes back on its own once its window renews.

## Several accounts and failover

- **Add another account..** Click the ChatGPT tile again, or run `magpie accounts add codex` again. Each account is listed under the provider.
- **Spread requests over them..** Open the provider’s row and tick every account to use. Smart routing, the default, sends requests to the account with quota to spare whose allowance renews soonest.
- **Fall back to another model..** The provider’s Fallback lists models to use when every account is out, rate limited or down, a model from another subscription or an API key included.

The routing modes are in [Get started](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start#routing).

## Switch back

Pick one of Claude Code’s own models on its row, or run:

```
magpie claude default
```

That takes magpie’s wiring out of Claude Code and puts back what it had. Disconnect on Claude Code’s row does the same.

> **Your claude.ai sign-in.** On a magpie model, Claude Code’s sign-in setting is magpie’s key by default: claude.ai is signed out for it, so `/usage` plan limits, connectors, voice and `/teleport` are off. Set it to claude.ai to keep them.

## The other way round: Claude in Codex

A Claude Pro or Max subscription works in Codex the same way. Sign in to Claude in magpie and pick a `claude/…` model for Codex. Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed.

```
magpie accounts add claude
magpie codex claude/claude-opus-5-5
```

See [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models) and [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions).

## FAQ

### Can I use my ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription in Claude Code?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in magpie and pick a `codex/…` model on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude codex/gpt-5.5`. magpie translates Claude Code’s requests for the GPT model and the replies back, tool calls included.

### Do I need an OpenAI API key?

No. magpie signs in on OpenAI’s own page, and Claude Code gets the gateway’s key. Your sign-in stays in magpie.

### Does it use my ChatGPT plan’s limits?

Yes. Requests are served on your ChatGPT account and count toward its usage limits. magpie’s status line shows each account’s 5h and 7d use under Claude Code’s prompt.

### Which model do Claude Code’s Haiku requests use?

The GPT model you picked, unless you give the haiku tier a model of its own with `magpie claude haiku <model>`.

### How do I go back to Claude’s own models?

Run `magpie claude default`, or pick one of Claude Code’s own models on its row in magpie.

### Do my requests go through a magpie server?

No. The gateway runs on your computer. Requests go from it to OpenAI; magpie has no server of its own in that path.

Using an API key instead? See [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

# Use Ollama or LM Studio models in Claude Code and Codex

Claude Code speaks Anthropic Messages and Codex speaks OpenAI Responses. A local model server speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, and some speak Anthropic Messages too. magpie sits between them on your computer, so Claude Code and Codex can run on the models you pulled in Ollama or loaded in LM Studio.

The gateway runs at `127.0.0.1:3425`. magpie points the agent at it and sends each request on to your server. When the server speaks the agent’s API itself, the request is passed on as it is. When it doesn’t, magpie translates the request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included.

### Ollama, LM Studio

Presets with their default ports and no key. magpie asks the server which models it has.

### oMLX, MLX-Serve

MLX servers for Apple silicon, also presets.

### Anything else

vLLM, llama.cpp’s server or any OpenAI-compatible URL, on this computer or another.

## Supported servers

These are under On this machine when you add a provider:

| Server | Default address | APIs magpie uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ollama | `http://localhost:11434` | Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages |
| LM Studio | `http://localhost:1234` | Chat Completions |
| oMLX | `http://localhost:8000` | Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages |
| MLX-Serve | `http://localhost:11234` | Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages |

So Claude Code on Ollama, oMLX or MLX-Serve sends its requests to the server as they are, and on LM Studio magpie translates them. Codex on oMLX or MLX-Serve goes as it is, and on Ollama or LM Studio magpie turns its Responses requests into Chat Completions.

## Set it up

1. **Start the server.** Pull or load a model in Ollama or LM Studio and leave the server running.
2. **Add it in magpie.** In the Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider and pick Ollama or LM Studio under On this machine. No key is needed. magpie asks the server which models it has, and they show as `ollama/…` or `lmstudio/…`.
3. **Pick the model for the agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the Claude Code or Codex row and choose the local one. magpie writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` or Codex’s `config.toml`. Start a new session to use it.

The same from a terminal:

```
ollama pull qwen3
magpie provider add ollama
magpie models                     # every model, as provider/model
magpie claude ollama/qwen3        # Claude Code
magpie codex ollama/qwen3         # Codex
```

Inside the agent, Claude Code’s and Codex’s `/model` list magpie’s models too, so you can move between a local model and a cloud one there. What changes in each agent’s config is in [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models#settings) and [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).

## Another port or another computer

If the server listens on another port, or runs on another computer such as a GPU box or a NAS, change Server address in the provider’s editor. Each of its URLs moves there and keeps its path.

```
magpie provider add lmstudio address=http://192.168.1.5:1234
magpie provider set ollama address=192.168.1.20:11434
magpie provider set ollama address=     # back to the default
```

A server behind HTTPS with a self-signed certificate can be reached with Don't check its certificate in the editor; it applies to that provider’s own hosts only.

## vLLM, llama.cpp and other servers

A server with no preset is added as Custom: paste its URL, such as `http://localhost:8080/v1`, and press Detect APIs. magpie sends the smallest request to Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini at that URL and keeps the ones that answer. The key can be left empty for a server that needs none.

## Context window

Agents plan around how long a request the model takes. Claude Code takes a model it doesn’t know for 200K, and Codex compacts a conversation at 90% of the window it is told. A local model is often loaded with a much smaller window, so tell magpie the real one: Context window under Advanced in the provider’s editor, for every model or one of them. magpie passes it on to the agents.

```
magpie provider set ollama context=32k
magpie provider set ollama context.qwen3=128k
```

## Masking

magpie’s [privacy masking](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/masking) replaces keys, tokens and other secrets with placeholders before a request leaves the gateway, a request to a local server too. When the model runs on your own computer or network, you can turn on Send requests unmasked in its editor, or run `magpie provider set ollama unmasked=yes`. It is your call: Ollama’s cloud models, or a relay you run locally, pass a request on to a vendor whatever the address.

## FAQ

### Can Claude Code use Ollama?

Yes. Add Ollama in magpie and pick one of its models for Claude Code. magpie writes the gateway’s address into Claude Code’s `settings.json`, and Ollama’s Anthropic-compatible API takes Claude Code’s requests as they are.

### Can Codex use Ollama or LM Studio?

Yes. Codex speaks only the Responses API, so magpie turns its requests into Chat Completions for Ollama and LM Studio, and the replies back, tool calls included. oMLX and MLX-Serve take Responses themselves.

### Do I need an API key?

No. The local presets take none. A server you secured with a key can have it in the provider’s editor.

### Can the model run on another computer?

Yes. Set the provider’s Server address to that computer, such as `http://192.168.1.20:11434`.

### Why does Claude Code fail on long conversations with a local model?

It assumes a model it doesn’t know takes 200K. Set the real Context window on the provider in magpie, and Claude Code and Codex compact before they reach it.

### How do I go back?

Pick one of the agent’s own models in magpie, or run `magpie claude default` or `magpie codex default`. What magpie wrote comes out, and what it replaced comes back.

Looking for cloud models? See [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models) and [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models). Stuck? Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models

# Use DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM or your Claude and ChatGPT subscription in OpenCode

OpenCode reaches a model through a provider in its config. magpie adds one provider, named `magpie`, that leads to a gateway on your computer. Every model you have in magpie is listed under it: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Qwen keys, and the models of a Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot sign-in.

The gateway runs at `127.0.0.1:3425`. OpenCode sends it OpenAI Chat Completions, and magpie passes each request on in the API its provider speaks, translating the request and the reply where they differ, streaming and tool calls included. OpenCode’s own providers stay as they were, next to magpie’s.

### Chinese models

DeepSeek, Kimi and Kimi Code, Zhipu GLM (pay as you go or Coding Plan), Z.ai, MiniMax and Qwen.

### Subscriptions

Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro and GitHub Copilot, signed in once in magpie.

### Anything else

Any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible URL and key, Ollama and LM Studio.

## Set it up

1. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax or Qwen, paste your API key and save. magpie asks the vendor which models it serves.
2. **Pick the model for OpenCode.** In the Agents tab, click the model on OpenCode’s row and choose one, such as `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`. magpie writes `"model": "magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"` into OpenCode’s config, with the `magpie` provider beside it.
3. **Or pick it in OpenCode.** Once the provider is there, magpie’s models are in OpenCode’s own `/models` list under `magpie`, so you can switch there too.

The same from a terminal:

```
magpie provider add deepseek sk-…
magpie models                                    # every model, as provider/model
magpie opencode deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro         # OpenCode's model
magpie opencode small deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash # its small_model
```

OpenCode’s `small_model` is a field of its own on the row, so it can run on a cheaper model than the main one.

> **Zhipu GLM Coding Plan.** When you add Zhipu GLM or Z.ai, pick the plan your key is for. A Coding Plan key has its own endpoints, and sent to the pay-as-you-go one it is told it has no balance.

## Subscriptions

Sign in once in magpie, from ＋ Add provider or a terminal, and the subscription’s models are listed under `magpie` in OpenCode like any other. No API key.

| Subscription | Models are | From a terminal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude (Pro, Max, Team) | `claude/…` | `magpie accounts add claude` `magpie opencode claude/claude-opus-5-5` |
| ChatGPT (Plus, Pro, Business) | `codex/…` | `magpie accounts add codex` `magpie opencode codex/gpt-5.5` |
| GitHub Copilot | `copilot/…` | `magpie accounts add copilot` |

Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed. Copilot gives you a code to enter on GitHub’s page. Several accounts of one subscription can share the load and fail over; see [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions#accounts).

## What changes in opencode.json

magpie writes to the config file OpenCode reads from its config folder, `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` when that is set and `~/.config/opencode` otherwise: the first of `opencode.jsonc`, `opencode.json` and `config.json` that exists, or a new `opencode.json`. It changes only these keys; your other settings stay.

| Key | Set to |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | `magpie/<provider>/<model>` |
| `small_model` | The same form, when you set one |
| `provider.magpie.npm` | `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` |
| `provider.magpie.options.baseURL` | `http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1` |
| `provider.magpie.options.apiKey` | The gateway’s key |
| `provider.magpie.models` | Every model magpie lists for OpenCode |

Each model carries its context window and output limit, so OpenCode knows when to compact; whether it takes images; its reasoning levels; and its price. magpie keeps the list up to date as you add providers and accounts. With OpenCode 2 installed, magpie writes OpenCode 2’s own keys instead: the provider under `providers.magpie` and the small model as `agents.title.model`. OpenCode in a WSL distro on Windows is set up the same way, in the distro’s `~/.config/opencode`.

## Reasoning levels and cost

- **Reasoning levels..** A model’s reasoning efforts are written as its variants in OpenCode, each one asking for that `reasoningEffort`. A model that offers fast processing, such as a GPT model from a ChatGPT plan, also gets a `fast` variant for each level.
- **Cost..** magpie writes each model’s price per million tokens, input, output, cache read and cache write, so OpenCode’s session cost counts, where without it every model costs 0.
- **Prompt caching..** magpie turns on OpenCode’s prompt cache key for its provider, so a provider that caches by it keeps the cache between turns.

## A shorter model list

By default OpenCode is shown every model you have in magpie. To show it only some providers or groups:

```
magpie visible opencode deepseek,claude   # only these providers
magpie visible opencode all               # every model again
```

A model left out of the list still answers when OpenCode asks for it by name.

## Switch back

On OpenCode’s row in magpie, the model picker lists OpenCode’s own providers too, the ones signed in in its `auth.json`. Pick one of them, or run:

```
magpie opencode default
```

It puts back the `model` and `small_model` OpenCode had before magpie, and takes the `magpie` provider out of the file.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek in OpenCode?

Add DeepSeek with your API key in magpie, then pick a DeepSeek model on OpenCode’s row in the Agents tab, or run magpie opencode deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro. magpie adds a magpie provider to `opencode.json` and sets the model.

### Can I use Kimi or GLM in OpenCode?

Yes. Add Kimi or Zhipu GLM in magpie and pick its model for OpenCode. For a GLM Coding Plan key, pick the Coding Plan when you add it, since it has its own endpoints.

### Can I use my Claude Pro or Max subscription in OpenCode?

Yes. Sign in to Claude in magpie (magpie accounts add claude) and pick a claude/… model for OpenCode. Requests on a Claude subscription run through the Claude Code installed on your computer, so keep it installed.

### Can I use my ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription in OpenCode?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in magpie (magpie accounts add codex) and pick a codex/… model, such as codex/gpt-5.5. Its reasoning levels show as the model’s variants in OpenCode.

### Which file does magpie change?

OpenCode’s config in ~/.config/opencode (or $OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR): the first of `opencode.json`c, `opencode.json` and config.json, or a new `opencode.json`. It sets model and `small_model` and adds provider.magpie; other settings stay.

### How do I switch back to OpenCode’s own model?

Pick one of OpenCode’s own models on its row in magpie, or run `magpie opencode default`. It puts back the model and `small_model` you had and removes magpie’s provider.

Other agents: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [OpenClaw on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openclaw), [OpenChamber on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openchamber). Stuck? Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/alternatives

# magpie, CC Switch and Claude Code Router compared

magpie, [CC Switch](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch) and [Claude Code Router](https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router) (CCR) all help you run AI coding agents on the providers and models you choose. They overlap, and each is good at something. This page puts them side by side, using each project’s own README for the other two and magpie’s source for magpie.

### CC Switch

A desktop app (Tauri 2) that manages twelve tools, from Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI to OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Pi and Kimi Code. It switches a tool’s provider by writing only the key fields of its config, backing it up first, and keeps MCP servers, skills and prompts for every tool in one place. An optional local routing mode converts API formats and fails over through a queue. It ships over 90 provider presets.

### Claude Code Router

A local model gateway and control plane at `127.0.0.1:3456`. Agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Kimi CLI, Kilo Code, OpenCode and Pi get one stable endpoint through an agent profile, and routing rules decide where each request goes: conditions on headers and bodies, rewrites, retries, credential pools and ordered fallbacks. It adds tools to models (vision, web search, MCP, browser automation) and logs every request with its cost. Desktop app, npm CLI with a web UI, or Docker.

### magpie

A menu bar (tray) app with a window, a TUI and a CLI. It points each agent at a local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425` that speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini and translates between them, so any agent can use any model, including a Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or Gemini sign-in. Several keys and sign-ins can stand behind one model, with failover before the agent sees an error.

## Side by side

|  | magpie | CC Switch as of its README, Nov 2026 | Claude Code Router as of its README, Nov 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Agents | Over 20, among them Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Goose, Crush, GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code, Kimi Code, Hermes Agent and Snow CLI | 12: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Pi, MiniMax Code, Kimi Code, Oh My Pi | Claude Code, Claude Design, Codex, Grok CLI, Kimi CLI, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Pi, ZCode, WorkBuddy, and compatible API clients |
| How it switches | Edits the one setting it changes in each agent’s config and points the agent at its local gateway | Direct: rewrites the key fields of the tool’s config. Routing (optional): a local proxy, default port 15721 | Local gateway; an agent profile connects the agent to it |
| Protocol translation | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini, both directions | In Routing mode, for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Grok Build | Providers in OpenAI Chat / Responses, Anthropic Messages or Gemini format behind one endpoint |
| Subscription sign-ins | Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro, GitHub Copilot, Gemini Code Assist, Antigravity | Accounts (Beta): GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, xAI (Grok), Kimi Code | Not stated (providers can import a local login where supported) |
| Routing and failover | Several keys and sign-ins behind one model; picks by intent, order, round robin, least used or quota; rests rate-limited accounts and fails over | Failover queue per tool with a circuit breaker (Routing mode); Aggregation puts several providers’ models in one list | Conditions on headers and bodies, prefixes, rewrites, retries, credential pools, key rotation, ordered fallback models |
| GUI and CLI | Menu bar / tray app with a window, TUI, CLI; Docker | Desktop app with a tray menu; CLI not stated | Desktop app; npm CLI with a browser UI; Docker |
| Platforms | macOS (signed and notarised), Windows, Linux | Windows 10+, macOS 12+ (signed and notarized), Linux (glibc 2.35+, WebKitGTK 4.1) | Windows, Linux (AppImage), macOS (Apple Silicon, Intel); signing not stated |
| License | MIT | MIT | MIT |

The CC Switch and Claude Code Router columns say only what their READMEs said in November 2026; where a README doesn’t say, the cell says “not stated”. Both projects move quickly, so check their pages for what has changed since.

## Which one fits

- **CC Switch.** fits when you mostly switch each tool between providers by hand and want its config left close to how you wrote it, with MCP servers, skills and prompts managed for every tool from one app. Its provider presets are the largest of the three, and it reaches tools the others don’t list, such as Claude Desktop, OpenClaw and Oh My Pi.
- **Claude Code Router.** fits when you want a gateway you can program: rules on headers and bodies, request rewrites, credential pools, client keys with their own quotas, and a log of every request with its cost. It also adds tools such as web search and browser automation to models that lack them, and runs headless from npm or Docker.
- **magpie.** fits when you use several agents and want each on a different model, Codex on DeepSeek and Claude Code on Kimi, say, or a Claude or ChatGPT subscription in another agent. Every agent goes through one translating gateway, and one model can be served by several accounts that take turns and fail over.

They can sit side by side. magpie’s gateway is an OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Gemini-compatible endpoint, so a tool that takes a custom base URL can use it as a provider.

## FAQ

### What is a CC Switch alternative?

magpie and Claude Code Router both cover part of what CC Switch does. magpie switches the model of each agent and runs every agent through one translating gateway with subscription sign-ins and failover; Claude Code Router is a programmable local gateway with routing rules and request logs.

### What is a claude-code-router alternative?

CC Switch, if you mostly want to switch each tool’s provider and keep its config as written; magpie, if you want a translating gateway for many agents with Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or Gemini sign-ins and accounts that fail over.

### CC Switch vs claude-code-router: what is the difference?

By their READMEs, CC Switch is a desktop manager that rewrites each tool’s config and offers an optional local routing proxy, while Claude Code Router is a local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3456` that agents connect to through profiles and that routes each request by rules.

### Does magpie rewrite my agent’s config like CC Switch?

It edits only the one setting it changes in each agent’s config file, keeping comments and order, and points the agent at its gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`. Picking the agent’s own model again puts the old value back.

### Is magpie a proxy like claude-code-router?

Yes, magpie runs a local gateway too. It speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini and translates between them, so Codex, which speaks only Responses, and Claude Code, which speaks only Messages, can use any provider’s model.

### Are all three free and open source?

Yes. magpie, CC Switch and Claude Code Router are each released under the MIT license.

Guides: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek

# DeepSeek in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

DeepSeek serves an OpenAI-compatible API and an Anthropic-compatible one. Add your key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use DeepSeek’s models through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`.

## Add DeepSeek

1. **Get an API key.** Create one at [platform.deepseek.com/api_keys](https://platform.deepseek.com/api_keys).
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick DeepSeek, paste the key and save. magpie asks DeepSeek which models it serves, such as `deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-v4-flash`.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a DeepSeek model.

```
magpie provider add deepseek sk-…
magpie models        # every model, as provider/model
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so DeepSeek’s are `deepseek/…`. Adding the preset again adds a second DeepSeek provider for another key; to spread requests over several keys, add them all to the one provider instead.

## Endpoints

DeepSeek has one plan, pay as you go, and magpie uses these endpoints for it:

| API | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic` |

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
magpie codex deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
magpie gemini model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
magpie opencode deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does DeepSeek’s Anthropic endpoint, so its requests are passed on as they are. Every tier (opus, sonnet, haiku) runs on the model you pick unless you give one its own. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. DeepSeek serves the Responses API itself, so Codex’s requests are passed on as they are. The model shows in Codex’s `/model` with its reasoning efforts. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. magpie points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants and cost. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Thinking, effort and the prompt cache

- **Thinking on tool turns..** DeepSeek’s Anthropic endpoint wants a thinking block on every assistant turn that calls a tool, and on turns that only answer tool results. When an agent’s history has none, magpie adds one, and turns a Claude `redacted_thinking` block into one. So a routing group can fall back from Claude to DeepSeek in the middle of a conversation.
- **Effort..** DeepSeek thinks at three levels, `low`, `high` and `max`, set in `output_config.effort`, and ignores `budget_tokens`. A token budget an agent sends is fitted to one of the three.
- **Prompt cache..** With several keys, magpie keeps a conversation on the same DeepSeek key for an hour after its last turn, so the next turn reads its prompt from DeepSeek’s cache instead of sending it uncached to another key.
- **Images..** magpie uploads each image an agent sends to DeepSeek’s API once and names it by its file id on later turns. `magpie provider set deepseek image-files=off` sends images inline on every turn instead.

## Balance and usage

The DeepSeek row shows your balance, read from DeepSeek: the total, what was granted and what you topped up. The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model that went through magpie.

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek in Claude Code?

Add your DeepSeek API key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, DeepSeek), then pick a DeepSeek model such as `deepseek-v4-pro` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`. magpie writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and passes its requests to DeepSeek’s Anthropic endpoint, `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`.

### Can Codex use DeepSeek?

Yes. DeepSeek serves the OpenAI Responses API that Codex speaks, so magpie passes Codex’s requests on as they are. Pick the model on Codex’s row or run `magpie codex deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`; it shows in Codex’s `/model` list.

### Do I need to set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to DeepSeek myself?

No. magpie points Claude Code at its own gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425` and keeps your DeepSeek key itself. Picking one of Claude Code’s own models again puts back what you had.

### Can I switch between Claude and DeepSeek in one conversation?

Yes. DeepSeek’s Anthropic endpoint wants a thinking block on tool-calling turns, and a conversation that started on Claude doesn’t have one it can read. magpie adds it, so a routing group can fall back from Claude to DeepSeek mid-conversation.

### Which reasoning effort does DeepSeek take?

DeepSeek thinks at three levels, low, high and max, set in `output_config.effort`, and ignores `budget_tokens`. magpie fits the level or token budget an agent asks for to one of those three.

### Can I use several DeepSeek keys?

Yes. Add them all to the DeepSeek provider and tick each one. magpie spreads requests over them, keeps a conversation on one key so its prompt cache is reused, and moves on when a key runs out of balance.

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi

# Kimi K2 and Kimi Code in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Kimi, from Moonshot AI, comes two ways: the Kimi API, paid as you go, and the Kimi Code membership, each with a global and a China endpoint. magpie has a preset for each of the four. Add a key once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and your other agents can use Kimi’s models through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`.

## Add Kimi

1. **Get a key.** For the Kimi API, from the Kimi platform’s API keys page; for Kimi Code, from the Kimi Code console. The table below links each.
2. **Add the provider.** In Providers, press ＋ Add provider and pick the preset that issued your key: Kimi, Kimi (China), Kimi Code or Kimi Code (China). Paste the key and save. magpie asks Kimi which models it serves.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, choose a Kimi model on the agent’s row: `kimi-k2.6` on the API, say, or `kimi-for-coding` on Kimi Code.

```
magpie provider add moonshot sk-…        # Kimi API (platform.kimi.ai)
magpie provider add moonshot-cn sk-…     # Kimi API, China (platform.kimi.com)
magpie provider add kimi-code sk-…       # Kimi Code membership
magpie provider add kimi-code-cn sk-…    # Kimi Code membership, China
```

Model ids are `provider/model`: `moonshot/kimi-k2.6`, `kimi-code/kimi-for-coding`. The models listed are the ones Kimi serves your key at the time.

## Plans and endpoints

| Preset | Plan | OpenAI Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages | Key from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kimi | Kimi API, pay as you go | `https://api.moonshot.ai/v1` | `https://api.moonshot.ai/anthropic` | [platform.kimi.ai](https://platform.kimi.ai/console/api-keys?aff=magpie) |
| Kimi (China) | Kimi API, pay as you go | `https://api.moonshot.cn/v1` | `https://api.moonshot.cn/anthropic` | [platform.kimi.com](https://platform.kimi.com/console/api-keys?aff=magpie) |
| Kimi Code | Kimi Code membership | `https://api.kimi.ai/coding/v1` | `https://api.kimi.ai/coding` | [kimi.ai/code/console](https://www.kimi.ai/code/console?aff=magpie) |
| Kimi Code (China) | Kimi Code membership | `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1` | `https://api.kimi.com/coding` | [kimi.com/code/console](https://www.kimi.com/code/console?aff=magpie) |

A key works only on the endpoints of the plan and region that issued it, so pick the preset that matches where you got it.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude moonshot/kimi-k2.6
magpie codex moonshot/kimi-k2.6
magpie gemini model moonshot/kimi-k2.6
magpie opencode kimi-code/kimi-for-coding
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does Kimi’s Anthropic endpoint, so its requests are passed on as they are. Every tier (opus, sonnet, haiku) runs on the model you pick unless you give one its own. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. Kimi serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not Responses, so magpie translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included. The model shows in Codex’s `/model` with its reasoning efforts. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. magpie points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants and cost. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Thinking

Some Kimi models always think: Kimi Code (China)’s K3.1 turns away a request that switches thinking off. When an agent asks for it off and the model refuses, magpie asks again with thinking left on, so the agent gets an answer rather than the error.

## Balance, windows and search

- **Kimi API..** The row shows your balance: in ¥ for Kimi (China), in $ for Kimi.
- **Kimi Code..** The row shows the membership’s windows, read from Kimi: the weekly allowance, shorter windows such as five hours, the monthly allowance and a booster pack’s balance.
- **Cost..** Kimi Code’s models are listed at $0, so magpie’s Usage tab prices their calls at the Kimi API’s price for the same model.
- **Web search..** A Kimi Code key searches the web through the membership’s own search endpoint, and magpie gives that search to Kimi Code models that can’t search by themselves.

## FAQ

### How do I use Kimi K2 in Codex?

Add your Kimi key in magpie, then pick a Kimi model such as `kimi-k2.6` on Codex’s row, or run `magpie codex moonshot/kimi-k2.6`. Kimi serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not the Responses API Codex speaks, so magpie translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included.

### Can I use my Kimi Code membership in Claude Code or Codex?

Yes. Add the Kimi Code preset (or Kimi Code (China)) with a key from the Kimi Code console. magpie sends requests to the membership’s own endpoints, `https://api.kimi.ai/coding` for Anthropic Messages and `https://api.kimi.ai/coding/v1` for Chat Completions, and shows the membership’s usage windows.

### Kimi or Kimi (China): which preset do I pick?

The one that issued your key. A key from platform.kimi.ai goes with Kimi (api.moonshot.ai); one from platform.kimi.com goes with Kimi (China) (api.moonshot.cn). Kimi Code has the same two: kimi.ai and kimi.com.

### Why does Kimi Code show a cost when the membership is prepaid?

Kimi Code’s model list prices its models at $0, so magpie prices each call at the Kimi API’s price for the same model. The figure shows what the work would have cost on the API; it isn’t charged.

### Can Kimi Code search the web for my agent?

Yes. A Kimi Code key searches the web through the membership’s own search endpoint, so a Kimi Code model that can’t search by itself is given magpie’s search on your plan.

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Kimi Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi-code). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm

# GLM Coding Plan in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Zhipu’s GLM models come from two places, Zhipu GLM at open.bigmodel.cn and Z.ai at api.z.ai, and each has two plans: pay as you go and the GLM Coding Plan. Add a key to magpie with its plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and your other agents can use GLM through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`.

## Add GLM

1. **Get a key.** From [open.bigmodel.cn](https://open.bigmodel.cn/usercenter/proj-mgmt/apikeys) for Zhipu GLM, or [z.ai](https://z.ai/manage-apikey/apikey-list) for Z.ai.
2. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** In Providers, press ＋ Add provider, pick Zhipu GLM or Z.ai, choose the plan your key is for (Pay as you go or Coding Plan), paste the key and save.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, choose a GLM model such as `glm-5.3` on the agent’s row.

```
magpie provider add zhipu sk-… plan=coding   # GLM Coding Plan (open.bigmodel.cn)
magpie provider add zai sk-… plan=coding     # GLM Coding Plan (z.ai)
magpie provider add zhipu sk-… plan=api      # pay as you go
```

> **Pick the plan your key is for.** A Coding Plan key has its own endpoints. Sent to the pay-as-you-go one, it is told it has no balance (429, code 1113). If that happens, magpie tries the Coding Plan endpoint, and when the key is served there it moves the provider to the plan’s endpoints. When both refuse, the error says what each said and what to change.

## Plans and endpoints

| Preset | Plan | OpenAI Chat Completions | OpenAI Responses | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zhipu GLM | Pay as you go | `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4` | — | `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/anthropic` |
| Zhipu GLM | Coding Plan | `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4` | `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/v1` | `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/anthropic` |
| Z.ai | Pay as you go | `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` | — | `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic` |
| Z.ai | Coding Plan | `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` | `https://api.z.ai/api/v1` | `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic` |

Both plans share the Anthropic endpoint, which bills the Coding Plan when the account has one. Each key on the provider says which plan it is for, so one provider can hold a pay-as-you-go key and a Coding Plan key, and each key’s requests, model list and windows are its own plan’s.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude zhipu/glm-5.3
magpie codex zhipu/glm-5.3
magpie gemini model zhipu/glm-5.3
magpie opencode zhipu/glm-5.3
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does GLM’s Anthropic endpoint, so its requests are passed on as they are. Every tier (opus, sonnet, haiku) runs on the model you pick unless you give one its own. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. The Coding Plan serves the Responses API itself, so Codex’s requests are passed on as they are; on pay as you go, magpie translates them to Chat Completions. The model shows in Codex’s `/model` with its reasoning efforts. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. magpie points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants and cost. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Thinking and effort

- **GLM-5.3 always thinks..** It turns away a request that switches thinking off. magpie asks again with thinking left on, so the agent gets an answer rather than the error.
- **Effort..** GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 take their reasoning level in `output_config.effort`, and magpie puts the agent’s level there.

## Usage windows and search

- **Coding Plan windows..** The row shows the plan’s windows, read from Zhipu or Z.ai: the hourly and weekly allowances, and the month’s MCP tool calls.
- **Web search..** With a Coding Plan key and no searcher chosen in Settings, magpie searches the web for GLM models through the plan’s own search service.

## FAQ

### How do I use the GLM Coding Plan in Claude Code?

Add Zhipu GLM (open.bigmodel.cn) or Z.ai (api.z.ai) in magpie, choose Coding Plan as the key’s plan, then pick a GLM model such as `glm-5.3` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude zhipu/glm-5.3`. Claude Code’s requests go to the Anthropic endpoint, which bills the Coding Plan when the account has one.

### Can Codex use GLM?

Yes. The GLM Coding Plan serves the OpenAI Responses API Codex speaks, so magpie passes Codex’s requests on as they are. On pay as you go, magpie translates Codex’s requests to Chat Completions. Run `magpie codex zhipu/glm-5.3` or pick it on Codex’s row.

### Why does my GLM Coding Plan key say insufficient balance (1113)?

A Coding Plan key sent to the pay-as-you-go endpoint, `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4`, is answered with 429 code 1113. magpie tries the Coding Plan endpoint, `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4`, and when the key is served there it moves the provider to the plan’s endpoints. Choosing Coding Plan when you add the key avoids it.

### Can I have a Coding Plan key and a pay-as-you-go key together?

Yes. Each key on a Zhipu GLM or Z.ai provider says which plan it is for. Its requests go to that plan’s endpoints, and its model list and usage windows are that plan’s.

### Zhipu GLM or Z.ai: which preset do I pick?

The one that issued your key: Zhipu GLM for a key from open.bigmodel.cn, Z.ai for a key from z.ai.

### Does GLM-5.3 work with thinking turned off?

GLM-5.3 always thinks and turns away a request that switches thinking off. magpie asks again with thinking left on, so the agent gets an answer.

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine

# Volcengine Ark Coding Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Volcengine Ark (火山方舟) is sold three ways: the Coding Plan, the Agent Plan and pay as you go. Each plan has endpoints of its own, and its quota is spent only there; a request to pay-as-you-go's /api/v3 is billed apart. Add the key in magpie with its plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other tools use Ark's Doubao, GLM, DeepSeek and Kimi models through magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add Volcengine Ark

1. **Get a key.** Create one on Ark's API key page (ark.volcengine.com). A plan's quota is spent only once the plan is subscribed on its own page.
2. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Volcengine Ark, set the key's plan to Coding Plan, Agent Plan or Pay as you go, and save.
3. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as ark-code-latest or doubao-seed-2.1-pro on a tool's row.

```
magpie claude volcengine/ark-code-latest
magpie codex volcengine/doubao-seed-2.1-pro
magpie opencode volcengine/glm-5.3
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Plan | Base URL (Chat Completions and Responses) | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coding Plan | `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/coding/v3` | `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/coding` |
| Agent Plan | `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/plan/v3` | `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/plan` |
| Pay as you go | `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/v3` | — (no Anthropic endpoint in the preset) |

The plans' paths carry their version and are used as written; no `/v1` goes on them. Each key in the provider names its own plan, so one provider can hold Coding Plan, Agent Plan and pay-as-you-go keys, and each key's requests go to its own plan's endpoint.

## The plans' models

Both plans list the same models. Their `/models` doesn't give them (the Coding Plan's lists Ark's general catalog, the Agent Plan's answers 404), so magpie uses the text models Ark's plan docs list, ark-code-latest first: ark-code-latest, doubao-seed-evolving, doubao-seed-2.1-pro, doubao-seed-2.1-lite, doubao-seed-2.0-mini, glm-5.3, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4.1-flash, kimi-k3 and kimi-k3.1-pro, among others. Which of them take images is the docs' word too: glm-5.3-flash and deepseek-v4.1-flash take an image as it is. A pay-as-you-go key reads Ark's own model list.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. The plans have Anthropic endpoints of their own (`/api/coding`, `/api/plan`), so requests go as they are and spend the plan. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. Ark's plan endpoints serve Responses themselves, so Codex's requests go as they are, and the models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : magpie writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Web search

Ark's Responses API runs the `web_search` tool itself, on pay as you go and both plans; its Chat API doesn't. So Codex's web search goes to Ark to run instead of being taken out of the request. `include` values Ark refuses are left out, so the request isn't turned away whole.

## Images and video

The Agent Plan also has Seedream image models (doubao-seedream-5-0-pro, doubao-seedream-5.0-flash) and Seedance video models (doubao-seedance-2.0, 2.0-fast, 2.0-mini, 2.5). Pick them in Settings → Images to use them through magpie's image and video tools. Ark has no OpenAI-shaped videos API, so magpie starts and polls Ark's asynchronous generation tasks.

## Usage windows

The Coding Plan and Agent Plan have 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows. Ark tells them only to the account's control plane (open.volcengineapi.com), never to the inference key, so the provider's editor asks for the account's AccessKey ID and Secret. With them, the row shows what is left of the plan; pay as you go has no windows.

## FAQ

### How do I use the Volcengine Ark Coding Plan in Claude Code?

Add Volcengine Ark in magpie with the key's plan set to Coding Plan, then pick a model such as ark-code-latest on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude volcengine/ark-code-latest. Requests go to the plan's Anthropic endpoint, https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/coding, and spend the plan.

### Why is a Coding Plan key billed as pay as you go?

A plan's quota is spent only at its own endpoints: /api/coding/v3 and /api/coding for the Coding Plan, /api/plan/v3 and /api/plan for the Agent Plan. /api/v3 is pay as you go. Set the key's plan in magpie and its requests go to the plan's endpoint.

### Does Volcengine Ark work in Codex?

Yes. The plan endpoints serve OpenAI Responses, so magpie passes Codex's requests through, and Ark runs web search itself. Run magpie codex volcengine/doubao-seed-2.1-pro, or pick it on Codex's row.

### How do I see what is left of an Ark plan?

Edit the Volcengine Ark provider and add the account's AccessKey ID and Secret. Ark tells the windows only through its control plane; the row then shows the 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows.

The same for other providers: [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Per-agent guides: [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud

# Tencent Cloud Token Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Tencent Cloud's models are on TokenHub: the Token Plan subscription (personal and enterprise) and pay as you go, each on keys of its own — an sk-tp- plan key, or TokenHub's own API key. Add one Tencent Cloud provider in magpie with each key's plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other tools use Hy, GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek and MiniMax through magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add Tencent Cloud

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Tencent Cloud, set the key's plan to Plan · China, Pay as you go · China, Pay as you go · Global, Enterprise plan · Global, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as tc-code-latest or glm-5.3 on a tool's row.

```
magpie claude tencent-cloud/tc-code-latest
magpie codex tencent-cloud/glm-5.3
magpie opencode tencent-cloud/kimi-k3
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Plan | Chat Completions and Responses | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Plan (personal, enterprise) · China | `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/plan/v3` | `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/plan/anthropic` |
| Pay as you go · China | `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1` | `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com` |
| Pay as you go · Global | `https://tokenhub-intl.tencentmaas.com/v1` | `https://tokenhub-intl.tencentmaas.com` |
| Enterprise · Singapore | `https://tokenhub-intl.tencentmaas.com/plan/v3` | `https://tokenhub-intl.tencentmaas.com/plan/anthropic` |

The personal and enterprise plans share endpoints; the key tells the plan. China is one region for both, so its models are the two plans' together; Singapore sells the enterprise plan alone. Each key in the provider names its plan, so pay-as-you-go and plan keys can share one provider.

The personal plan used to be at `api.lkeap.cloud.tencent.com` until Tencent moved it to TokenHub. A provider saved at the old host is moved to the new one.

## The plans' models

The plans give no model list of their own, and the public catalog names only their Hy models, so magpie gives the models from Tencent's plan docs: tc-code-latest, auto, glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, kimi-k3, kimi-k2.7-code, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4.1-flash, minimax-m3, hy4-preview, hy3, mimo-v2.6-pro, among others. tc-code-latest is whichever model the console has picked. A pay-as-you-go key reads TokenHub's `/v1/models`, which has other makers' models such as Qwen too.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. The plan and pay as you go both have Anthropic endpoints, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. TokenHub's plan and pay as you go both serve Responses, so Codex's requests go as they are. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : magpie writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Enterprise quota

The enterprise plan's cycle quota (credits on 专业套餐, tokens on 轻享套餐) is told only to Tencent Cloud's API, signed with the account's SecretId and SecretKey, never to the plan key. Add them in the provider's editor, and magpie's Usage page shows a card for each enterprise plan the SecretId can see: what the cycle has used and when it resets. The personal plan has no API for its usage, only the console; pay as you go has no windows.

## FAQ

### How do I use the Tencent Cloud Token Plan in Claude Code?

Add Tencent Cloud in magpie with the key's plan set to Plan · China, then pick tc-code-latest or glm-5.3 on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude tencent-cloud/tc-code-latest. Requests go to the plan's Anthropic endpoint, https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/plan/anthropic.

### What is the difference between a Token Plan key and a TokenHub pay-as-you-go key?

A plan key starts with sk-tp- and works only at the plan endpoints under /plan; pay as you go uses TokenHub's own API key at /v1. Set each key's plan in magpie; both can share one provider.

### Does the personal plan's old host api.lkeap.cloud.tencent.com still work?

Tencent moved the personal plan to tokenhub.tencentmaas.com. A provider in magpie saved at the old host is moved to the new one by itself.

### Can magpie show what is left of a Tencent Cloud plan?

For the enterprise plan, yes: add the account's SecretId and SecretKey in the provider's editor, and the Usage page shows the cycle's use and its reset. The personal plan has no API for it; see Tencent Cloud's console.

The same for other providers: [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Tencent's own coding agent: [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codebuddy). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan

# Baidu Qianfan Token Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Baidu Qianfan (百度千帆) has two Token Plans, personal and enterprise, and pay as you go, each with endpoints and keys of its own. Add Baidu Qianfan in magpie with each key's plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other tools use Qianfan's DeepSeek and GLM through magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add Baidu Qianfan

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Baidu Qianfan, set the key's plan to Token Plan Personal, Token Plan Enterprise, Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as qianfan-code-latest or deepseek-v4-pro on a tool's row.

```
magpie claude baidu-qianfan/qianfan-code-latest
magpie codex baidu-qianfan/deepseek-v4-pro
magpie opencode baidu-qianfan/glm-5.3
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Plan | Chat Completions and Responses | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Plan personal | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2/tokenplan/personal` | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic/tokenplan/personal` |
| Token Plan enterprise | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2/tokenplan/team` | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic/tokenplan/team` |
| Pay as you go | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2` | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic` |

Each plan's key works at its own endpoints. Each key in the provider names its plan, so personal, enterprise and pay-as-you-go keys can share one provider, and each key's requests go to its own plan's endpoint.

## The plans' models

The plans' `/models` answers 404, so magpie gives the models from both plans' docs: qianfan-code-latest, deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-pro-0813, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, glm-5.2, glm-5.1, among others. deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v3.2 and glm-5 are the enterprise plan's alone. qianfan-code-latest is whichever model the console has picked. A pay-as-you-go key reads Qianfan's `/v2/models`.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Qianfan's plans and pay as you go have Anthropic endpoints, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. Qianfan's plan endpoints serve Responses too, so Codex's requests go as they are. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : magpie writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use the Baidu Qianfan Token Plan in Claude Code?

Add Baidu Qianfan in magpie with the key's plan set to Token Plan Personal or Enterprise, then pick qianfan-code-latest on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude baidu-qianfan/qianfan-code-latest. Requests go to the plan's Anthropic endpoint, such as https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic/tokenplan/personal.

### Which model is qianfan-code-latest?

The one you picked for the plan in Qianfan's console. Change it there; the name in magpie and your tools stays the same.

### Do the personal and enterprise plans have the same models?

Mostly. deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v3.2 and glm-5 are the enterprise plan's alone; deepseek-v4-pro, glm-5.3 and the others are in both.

### Does Baidu Qianfan work in Codex?

Yes. Qianfan's plan endpoints serve OpenAI Responses, so magpie passes Codex's requests through. Run magpie codex baidu-qianfan/deepseek-v4-pro, or pick it on Codex's row.

The same for other providers: [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine), [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow

# SiliconFlow in Claude Code and Codex

SiliconFlow (硅基流动) serves open models such as DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Qwen on one API key, over OpenAI's Chat Completions. Claude Code wants Anthropic Messages and Codex wants Responses, and SiliconFlow serves neither; magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425 converts between them, so these tools use SiliconFlow's models directly.

## Add SiliconFlow

1. **Add the provider.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick SiliconFlow, set the key to China or Global, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro on a tool's row.

```
magpie claude siliconflow/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
magpie codex siliconflow/zai-org/GLM-5.3
magpie opencode siliconflow/moonshotai/Kimi-K3
```

## China and Global

| Site | Chat Completions | Console |
| --- | --- | --- |
| China | `https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1` | cloud.siliconflow.cn |
| Global | `https://api.siliconflow.com/v1` | cloud.siliconflow.com |

The Global site is another account, with keys and a balance (in $) of its own; a China key doesn't work there. Each key in the provider names its site, so keys from both can share one provider.

## Models

SiliconFlow's model names carry their maker, and go into magpie and your tools as written: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, zai-org/GLM-5.3, moonshotai/Kimi-K3, moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code, Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0. magpie takes their names, context and prices from models.dev's siliconflow catalog. On the command line, write `siliconflow/` then the name.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which this provider doesn't serve. magpie converts each request to Chat Completions and the reply back, reasoning included. [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses. It has no Responses, so magpie converts to Chat Completions; Codex's custom tools such as `apply_patch` go to the model as functions, and its calls come back as Codex can run them. [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie converts it to Chat Completions. [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so requests go as they are. [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Balance

SiliconFlow retired its balance query, `/v1/user/info`, on 2026-08-14 (it answers 410) with nothing in its place yet, and its old granted balance is a voucher now. So magpie's usage card says where the balance is shown instead of an amount, and its button opens that site's console. A key refused for itself (401) is said as it came.

## FAQ

### How do I use SiliconFlow in Claude Code?

Add SiliconFlow in magpie with your key, then pick a model such as deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude siliconflow/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro. SiliconFlow has no Anthropic endpoint, so magpie converts Claude Code's requests to Chat Completions.

### Does SiliconFlow work in Codex?

Yes. SiliconFlow has Chat Completions only, so magpie converts Codex's Responses requests, custom tools like apply_patch included. Run magpie codex siliconflow/zai-org/GLM-5.3.

### Does a China key work on the Global site?

No. cloud.siliconflow.com is another account, with its own keys and balance. Set each key's site to China or Global in magpie.

### Why doesn't magpie show my SiliconFlow balance?

SiliconFlow retired its balance API on 2026-08-14 and has no new one yet. magpie's card takes you to the console, where the balance and vouchers are shown.

The same for other providers: [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope), [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope

# ModelScope in Claude Code and Codex

ModelScope's (魔搭) API-Inference takes a ModelScope account's access token as its key and serves models such as Qwen and GLM over Chat Completions and Responses. Add ModelScope in magpie, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode use them through magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add ModelScope

1. **Add the provider.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick ModelScope, use your ModelScope access token as the key, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on a tool's row.

```
magpie claude modelscope/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
magpie codex modelscope/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.6
magpie opencode modelscope/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507
```

## Endpoint and token

| API | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api-inference.modelscope.cn/v1` |
| Responses | `https://api-inference.modelscope.cn/v1` |

The key is a ModelScope account's access token, made at modelscope.cn/my/myaccesstoken. ModelScope is not Alibaba Cloud's DashScope: a DashScope key goes in the [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) provider, and neither works on the other. A provider added by hand at api-inference.modelscope.cn is taken as ModelScope too.

## Models

ModelScope's model names carry their organisation, written as they are: Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507, Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507, ZhipuAI/GLM-4.6, ZhipuAI/GLM-4.5, among others. magpie takes their names and context from models.dev's modelscope catalog. On the command line, write `modelscope/` then the name.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which this provider doesn't serve. magpie converts each request to Chat Completions and the reply back, reasoning included. [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses. It serves Responses too, so Codex's requests go as they are. [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie converts it to Chat Completions. [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so requests go as they are. [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Images

ModelScope draws through async tasks of its own: a request starts a task and answers its task_id, which is asked about until it succeeds or fails. It runs one task of a user's at a time and answers bursts with 429, so magpie asks for one image at a time, waits a moment when it is busy, and hands the result to your tool as an image it can read.

## FAQ

### How do I use ModelScope in Claude Code?

Add ModelScope in magpie with your access token as the key, then pick Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude modelscope/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct. ModelScope has no Anthropic endpoint, so magpie converts to Chat Completions.

### Where do I get a ModelScope key?

ModelScope uses your account's access token, made at modelscope.cn/my/myaccesstoken. Paste it into magpie's ModelScope provider.

### Is ModelScope the same as Alibaba's DashScope?

No. ModelScope's API-Inference is at api-inference.modelscope.cn on a ModelScope access token; DashScope takes an Alibaba Cloud key and is magpie's Qwen provider.

### Does ModelScope work in Codex?

Yes. ModelScope serves Responses, so magpie passes Codex's requests through. Run magpie codex modelscope/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.6.

The same for other providers: [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow), [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud

# Huawei Cloud MaaS Token Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Huawei Cloud ModelArts MaaS's Token Plan is for personal accounts in 西南-贵阳一 (Guiyang) and serves GLM, Kimi and DeepSeek over Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages. Add Huawei Cloud in magpie with the plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode use them through magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add Huawei Cloud

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Huawei Cloud MaaS, set the key's plan to Token Plan or Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as glm-5.3 on a tool's row.

```
magpie claude huaweicloud/glm-5.3
magpie codex huaweicloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash
magpie opencode huaweicloud/kimi-k2.6
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Plan | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Plan | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/plan/v2` | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/plan/anthropic` |
| Pay as you go | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/openai/v1` | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/anthropic` |

The Token Plan's quota is spent only at the endpoints under `/plan`, so magpie uses the plan's by default; pay as you go bills apart. Both take a MaaS API key, made under the ModelArts console's authentication management. Each key in the provider names its plan. Neither serves Responses.

## Models

Until its list is fetched, magpie gives the plan's models: glm-5.3, glm-5.1, kimi-k2.6, deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, lowercase as Huawei's OpenClaw page writes them. Once the list is in, Huawei's own list is the one served.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which the plan serves, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses, which Huawei Cloud doesn't serve, so magpie converts to Chat Completions; custom tools such as `apply_patch` go to the model as functions and come back as Codex can run them. See [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie translates at the local gateway. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : magpie writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use the Huawei Cloud Token Plan in Claude Code?

Add Huawei Cloud MaaS in magpie with the key's plan set to Token Plan, then pick glm-5.3 on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude huaweicloud/glm-5.3. Requests go to the plan's Anthropic endpoint, https://api.modelarts-maas.com/plan/anthropic.

### Does Huawei Cloud MaaS work in Codex?

Yes. Huawei Cloud has no Responses endpoint, so magpie converts Codex's requests to Chat Completions, custom tools included. Run magpie codex huaweicloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash.

### Why the endpoints under /plan?

The Token Plan's quota is spent only at /plan/v2 and /plan/anthropic; requests to pay as you go's /openai/v1 bill apart. magpie uses the plan's endpoints by default.

### Which models does the Huawei Cloud Token Plan have?

magpie gives glm-5.3, glm-5.1, kimi-k2.6, deepseek-v4.1-flash and deepseek-v4-flash until Huawei's list is fetched, and then serves that list.

The same for other providers: [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud), [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan), [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

# Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Xiaomi's MiMo platform has a Token Plan and pay as you go. A Token Plan's tp- key works only at its region's own host (China, Singapore or Europe); pay as you go is api.xiaomimimo.com. Each serves Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages, so Claude Code's, Codex's and OpenCode's requests go as they are, with magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425 routing them and holding the key.

## Add Xiaomi MiMo

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Xiaomi MiMo, set the key's plan to Plan · China, Plan · Singapore, Plan · Europe, Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as mimo-v2.6-pro on a tool's row.

```
magpie claude xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro
magpie codex xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro
magpie opencode xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash
```

## Regions and endpoints

| Plan | Chat Completions and Responses | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Plan · China | `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |
| Token Plan · Singapore | `https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |
| Token Plan · Europe | `https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |
| Pay as you go | `https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://api.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |

A Token Plan's tp- key is spent only at the host of the region it was bought in. Each key in the provider names its region, so keys from several regions and pay as you go can share one provider. Plans and their keys are at platform.xiaomimimo.com/token-plan.

## Models

Each region names its own catalog: a plan's region lists the plan's models before Xiaomi's public catalog, and pay as you go uses the public one alone. The main chat models are mimo-v2.6-pro, mimo-v2.6-flash, mimo-v2.5-pro and mimo-v2.5. The plan catalogs price their models at $0, which magpie doesn't take as a price, so a pay-as-you-go call is counted at Xiaomi's own prices, not at $0. The model list is read from api.xiaomimimo.com.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Each MiMo region has an Anthropic endpoint, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. Each MiMo region serves Responses, so Codex's requests go as they are. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : magpie writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## The MiMo app subscription

This page is about the platform's API keys. The MiMo app subscription you sign in to with a Xiaomi account (mimo-app) is another thing: it moved out of magpie's built-ins into the community plugin `@magpie-community/opencode-mimo-auth`; install it from magpie's Plugins page and sign in.

## FAQ

### How do I use Xiaomi MiMo in Claude Code?

Add Xiaomi MiMo in magpie with your tp- key's region (say Plan · China), then pick mimo-v2.6-pro on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro. Requests go to that region's Anthropic endpoint, such as https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic.

### Does a MiMo Token Plan key work in another region?

No. A tp- key is spent only at its own region's host. Set each key's region in magpie; keys from several regions can share one provider.

### Does MiMo work in Codex?

Yes. Each MiMo region serves OpenAI Responses, so magpie passes Codex's requests through. Run magpie codex xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro.

### Can I use the MiMo app subscription too?

Yes, but not in this provider. The MiMo app subscription signed in with a Xiaomi account is served by the community plugin @magpie-community/opencode-mimo-auth; install it from magpie's Plugins page.

The same for other providers: [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud), [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).
