Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun

# StepFun Step Plan in Claude Code and Codex

StepFun has two sites with separate accounts: platform.stepfun.com in China and platform.stepfun.ai internationally. Each has a Step Plan and pay as you go; the Step Plan is served at its own step_plan endpoints, and its key is refused at pay as you go's. Add the provider for your site in magpie with the key's plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode use Step's models through magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add StepFun

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick StepFun or StepFun (China), set the key's plan to Step Plan or Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as step-5-preview on a tool's row.

An international account is StepFun (provider id `stepfun`); a China account is StepFun (China) (`stepfun-cn`).

```
magpie claude stepfun-cn/step-5-preview
magpie codex stepfun-cn/step-3.7-flash
magpie opencode stepfun/step-5-preview
```

## Sites, plans and endpoints

| Site and plan | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| China · Step Plan | `https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan` |
| China · Pay as you go | `https://api.stepfun.com/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.com` |
| International · Step Plan | `https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan` |
| International · Pay as you go | `https://api.stepfun.ai/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.ai` |

A Step Plan key works only at the endpoints under `step_plan` and is refused at pay as you go's, so magpie sends each request by the plan its key names. A Step Plan key and a pay-as-you-go key on one site can share one provider. Neither serves Responses.

## Models

The Step Plan catalogs' chat models are step-5-preview, step-3.7-flash, step-3.5-flash and step-3.5-flash-2603; the China Step Plan has step-router-v1 too. Pay as you go adds the speech models stepaudio-2.5-asr, stepaudio-2.5-tts and step-tts-2.

## Balance and Step Plan windows

- **Balance.** : magpie reads `/v1/accounts` with the API key, in yuan on the China site and dollars on the international one.
- **Step Plan windows.** : the 5-hour and weekly windows and the month's credits are told only to a sign-in on StepFun's platform, not to a key. Sign in on the platform in your own browser, run magpie's bookmarklet on that page, and paste what it copies into magpie. magpie then renews the sign-in and reads the windows itself; it is kept in stepfun-auth.json beside providers.json, readable by you alone. Two providers on one site can be two accounts, each with its own windows.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Both StepFun sites have Anthropic endpoints, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. StepFun doesn't serve Responses, so magpie converts Codex's requests to Chat Completions, custom tools such as `apply_patch` included. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : magpie writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use the StepFun Step Plan in Claude Code?

Add StepFun or StepFun (China) in magpie with the key's plan set to Step Plan, then pick step-5-preview on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude stepfun/step-5-preview. Requests go to https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan (api.stepfun.com in China).

### Why is my Step Plan key refused at /v1?

A Step Plan key works only at the endpoints under step_plan; pay as you go's /v1 refuses it. Set the key's plan to Step Plan in magpie and requests go to /step_plan/v1.

### Does StepFun work in Codex?

Yes. StepFun has no Responses endpoint, so magpie converts Codex's requests to Chat Completions. Run magpie codex stepfun/step-3.7-flash.

### Can magpie show the Step Plan's 5-hour and weekly windows?

Yes, once the platform's sign-in is brought over: sign in on platform.stepfun.ai or .com in your browser, run magpie's bookmarklet and paste what it copies into magpie. The balance needs only the key.

The same for other providers: [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo), [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud), [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat

# Meituan LongCat in Claude Code and Codex

LongCat is Meituan's model platform, serving its own LongCat models at api.longcat.chat. Accounts from longcat.chat and longcat.ai share that host: Chat Completions and Responses under /openai/v1, Anthropic Messages under /anthropic. Add LongCat in magpie, and Claude Code's, Codex's, Gemini CLI's and OpenCode's requests go as they are, with magpie's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425 routing them and holding the key.

## Add LongCat

1. **Add the provider.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick LongCat, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as LongCat-2.0 on a tool's row.

Keys are made at longcat.chat/platform/api_keys.

```
magpie claude longcat/LongCat-2.0
magpie codex longcat/LongCat-2.0
magpie opencode longcat/LongCat-2.5-Preview
```

## Endpoints

| API | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1` |
| Responses | `https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1` |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://api.longcat.chat/anthropic` |
| /models | `https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1/models` |

Both take the key as `Authorization: Bearer`; with `x-api-key` alone LongCat answers missing_api_key, and magpie's Anthropic requests carry the key in both x-api-key and a Bearer by default, so they pass. An entry another app has at these endpoints is imported as LongCat.

## Models

magpie gives LongCat-2.0 and LongCat-2.5-Preview, then reads LongCat's list from `/openai/v1/models` and serves that. Model names are case-sensitive; write them as the list does.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. LongCat has an Anthropic endpoint, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. LongCat serves Responses, so Codex's requests go as they are. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; magpie points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : magpie writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use LongCat in Claude Code?

Add LongCat in magpie with your longcat.chat platform key, then pick LongCat-2.0 on Claude Code's row, or run magpie claude longcat/LongCat-2.0. Requests go to https://api.longcat.chat/anthropic.

### Does LongCat work in Codex?

Yes. LongCat serves Responses under /openai/v1, so magpie passes Codex's requests through. Run magpie codex longcat/LongCat-2.0.

### Why does Claude Code get missing_api_key from LongCat directly?

LongCat takes the key only as Authorization: Bearer and refuses x-api-key alone. Through magpie, the key goes in both x-api-key and a Bearer by default.

### Does a longcat.ai account work?

Yes. longcat.chat and longcat.ai accounts share api.longcat.chat; add LongCat in magpie for either.

The same for other providers: [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun), [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen

# Qwen in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Alibaba serves Qwen through DashScope, on Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, Bailian and Qwen Cloud, pay as you go or on a Token Plan. Every one of them speaks OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages. Add your key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Qwen through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`.

## Add Qwen

1. **Get a key.** Pay as you go: [Model Studio](https://modelstudio.console.alibabacloud.com/?tab=playground#/api-key) (international) or [Bailian](https://bailian.console.aliyun.com/?tab=model#/api-key) (China). A Token Plan’s key comes from its own plan page.
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick the Qwen preset your key is from (the table below), paste the key and save. magpie asks the endpoint which models it serves.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Qwen model such as `qwen3.8-max`.

```
magpie provider add qwen sk-…                     # Model Studio, international
magpie provider add qwen-cn sk-…                  # Bailian, China
magpie provider add bailian-token-plan sk-sp-…    # Bailian Token Plan
magpie provider add qwencloud sk-ws-… region=us-east-1
```

> **Each key works on its own host only.** A Token Plan key (`sk-sp-…`) is refused by pay-as-you-go endpoints and by the other Token Plans, and a Qwen Cloud key is refused outside its region. If a request comes back 401, check that the key sits under the preset it was made for.

## Plans and endpoints

| Preset | Plan and key | Endpoints (Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen qwen | pay as you go, international (Model Studio) | `https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen (China) qwen-cn | pay as you go, China (Bailian) | `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen Token Plan qwen-token-plan | subscription, `sk-sp-` | `https://token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Bailian Token Plan bailian-token-plan | subscription, `sk-sp-` | `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen Cloud qwencloud | pay as you go, `sk-ws-`, six regions, Singapore the default | `https://{region}.maas.qwencloudapi.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://{region}.maas.qwencloudapi.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen Cloud Token Plan qwencloud-token-plan | subscription, `sk-sp-`, Singapore | `https://token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com/apps/anthropic` |

When a Token Plan’s host gives no model list, magpie offers the plan’s text models as its overview lists them: auto, qwen3.8-max, qwen3.8-flash, qwen3.7-max, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.6-flash, and the DeepSeek and GLM models the plan includes. The Bailian Token Plan also serves a decision model that can classify turns for [intent routing](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/intent).

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude qwen/qwen3.8-max
magpie codex qwen/qwen3.8-max
magpie gemini model qwen/qwen3.7-plus
magpie opencode qwen/qwen3.8-max
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does Qwen’s Anthropic endpoint, so its requests are passed on as they are. Every tier (opus, sonnet, haiku) runs on the model you pick unless you give one its own. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. DashScope serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not Responses, so magpie translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included. The model shows in Codex’s `/model` with its reasoning efforts. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. magpie points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants and cost. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

Qwen Code is one of the agents magpie connects too: its row takes Qwen’s models or any other vendor’s.

## Thinking and images

- **Whole replies..** DashScope answers a thinking Qwen model only as a stream, and turns away a request for one whole reply. When an agent or a routing group’s classifier asks for one, magpie asks DashScope for a stream and gives the agent the whole reply, thinking included.
- **Models that always think..** Some models on DashScope refuse to have thinking turned off, such as its `glm-5.3`. When an agent asks for it off and the model refuses, magpie asks again with thinking left on.
- **Images..** The Qwen-Image and `wan2.7-image` models draw through DashScope’s own image API, on any of the six presets. Choose one in magpie’s Settings → Models → Images. Give a size as `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, at most 2048×2048.

## Balance and usage

magpie shows no balance or plan card for Qwen: DashScope has no API for a key’s balance, and neither Token Plan has one for its credits, which the plan’s subscription page in Alibaba’s console shows. The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model that went through magpie.

## FAQ

### How do I use Qwen in Claude Code?

Add your key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, then the Qwen preset your key is from), then pick a Qwen model such as `qwen3.8-max` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude qwen/qwen3.8-max`. magpie writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and passes its requests to DashScope’s Anthropic endpoint.

### Can Codex use Qwen, Qwen3 Coder included?

Yes. magpie lists the models DashScope gives your key, coder models included, and Codex can use any of them: magpie translates Codex’s Responses requests to Chat Completions and the replies back. Pick the model on Codex’s row or run `magpie codex qwen/qwen3.8-max`; it shows in Codex’s `/model` list.

### Which preset do I pick for my key?

The one whose site the key is from. A Token Plan key (`sk-sp-…`) works only on its own plan’s host, and a Qwen Cloud pay-as-you-go key (`sk-ws-…`) only in its own region, so a key added to another preset is turned away with 401.

### Can Qwen Code use other models?

Yes. Qwen Code is one of the agents magpie connects, so its row in the Agents tab takes any model you have added, Qwen’s or another vendor’s.

### Why does a Qwen request without streaming work in magpie?

DashScope turns away a thinking Qwen model asked for one whole reply (`enable_thinking` must be false for non-streaming calls). magpie asks for it streamed and hands the agent the whole reply, thinking included.

### Does magpie show my Token Plan credits?

No. Neither Token Plan has an API for its credits; the plan’s subscription page in Alibaba’s console shows them. magpie’s Usage tab still counts the tokens each agent spent.

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Qwen Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen-code). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax

# MiniMax and the MiniMax Coding Plan in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

MiniMax serves an OpenAI-compatible Chat API and an Anthropic-compatible one, on a global site and a China site, for pay-as-you-go keys and Coding Plan keys alike. Add your key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use models such as `MiniMax-M3` and `MiniMax-M2.7` through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`.

## Add MiniMax

1. **Get a key.** Create one at [platform.minimax.io](https://platform.minimax.io/user-center/basic-information/interface-key), or [platform.minimaxi.com](https://platform.minimaxi.com/user-center/basic-information/interface-key) for the China site. A Coding Plan key starts with `sk-cp-`.
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick MiniMax or MiniMax (China), paste the key and save. A pay-as-you-go key and a Coding Plan key go in the same way.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a MiniMax model.

```
magpie provider add minimax sk-…        # platform.minimax.io
magpie provider add minimax-cn sk-cp-…  # Coding Plan, platform.minimaxi.com
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Preset | Site | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MiniMax minimax | platform.minimax.io | `https://api.minimax.io/v1` | `https://api.minimax.io/anthropic` |
| MiniMax (China) minimax-cn | platform.minimaxi.com | `https://api.minimaxi.com/v1` | `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic` |

The Coding Plan uses the same endpoints as pay as you go; the key decides which one a request is billed to. A global key and a China key are different accounts, so each goes under its own site’s preset.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude minimax/MiniMax-M3
magpie codex minimax/MiniMax-M3
magpie gemini model minimax/MiniMax-M2.7
magpie opencode minimax/MiniMax-M3
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does MiniMax’s Anthropic endpoint, so its requests are passed on as they are. Every tier (opus, sonnet, haiku) runs on the model you pick unless you give one its own. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. MiniMax serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not Responses, so magpie translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included. The model shows in Codex’s `/model` with its reasoning efforts. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. magpie points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants and cost. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

MiniMax Code is one of the agents magpie connects too: its row takes MiniMax’s models or any other vendor’s.

## Thinking and effort

- **Interleaved thinking..** MiniMax’s Chat API gives a model’s thinking in the reply text, between `<think>` tags, and wants it back there on later turns. magpie hands it to the agent as thinking and puts it back where MiniMax expects it.
- **Effort..** `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` and its preview think at levels from low to max. magpie sends the level an agent asks for in `output_config.effort`, as MiniMax Code does, so it isn’t lost to a token budget.
- **Models that always think..** `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` refuses to have thinking turned off. When an agent asks for it off, magpie asks again with thinking left on, so the agent gets an answer rather than the error.

## Coding Plan windows and usage

- **Coding Plan windows..** A Coding Plan key’s row shows what is left of each window MiniMax reports, a rolling one and a weekly one, read from MiniMax. Models draw on the general bucket; a bucket metered apart, such as video, shows as a count, like 4 / 5. A pay-as-you-go key has no windows and no card.
- **Routing..** With several Coding Plan keys, magpie weighs them by their windows and rests one that has used a window up until it resets.
- **Usage..** The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model that went through magpie.

## FAQ

### How do I use MiniMax M2.7 or M3 in Claude Code?

Add your MiniMax key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, MiniMax or MiniMax (China)), then pick a model such as `MiniMax-M3` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude minimax/MiniMax-M3`. magpie writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and passes its requests to MiniMax’s Anthropic endpoint, `https://api.minimax.io/anthropic`.

### How do I use the MiniMax Coding Plan?

Add the Coding Plan key (`sk-cp-…`) to the MiniMax preset of the site you bought it on, the same as a pay-as-you-go key. magpie tells the two apart by what MiniMax says about the key, and shows a Coding Plan key’s usage windows on its row.

### Can Codex use MiniMax?

Yes. MiniMax serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not Responses, so magpie translates Codex’s requests and MiniMax’s replies. Pick the model on Codex’s row or run `magpie codex minimax/MiniMax-M3`; it shows in Codex’s `/model` list.

### Can MiniMax Code use other models?

Yes. MiniMax Code is one of the agents magpie connects, so its row in the Agents tab takes any model you have added, MiniMax’s or another vendor’s.

### Why does MiniMax’s thinking show up in the text?

MiniMax’s Chat API puts a model’s thinking in the reply text between `<think>` tags. magpie takes it out and gives it to the agent as thinking, then puts it back on the next turns, where MiniMax wants it.

### Can I use several MiniMax keys?

Yes. Add them all to the MiniMax provider and tick each one. magpie spreads requests over them, and weighs and rests Coding Plan keys by their windows, so a key that has used up its window sits out until it resets.

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

# OpenRouter in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

OpenRouter sells many vendors’ models behind one key and serves them on OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages. Add the key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use any OpenRouter model through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent on a model of its own.

## Add OpenRouter

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys).
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick OpenRouter, paste the key and save. magpie asks OpenRouter which models it serves.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose an OpenRouter model such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`.

```
magpie provider add openrouter sk-…
magpie provider test openrouter
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so OpenRouter’s read `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`: the provider, then OpenRouter’s own id. The key is kept in magpie’s settings; magpie doesn’t take it from your shell.

OpenRouter documents two optional headers that credit an app in its rankings, `HTTP-Referer` and `X-OpenRouter-Title`. magpie doesn’t send them. The provider editor’s Headers field offers them if you want your requests credited.

## Endpoints

| API | Base URL | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | the model list, requests to non-Claude models, image models |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | Claude Code’s requests, and Claude models from any agent |
| Decisions | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | decision models for [intent routing](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/intent) |

magpie doesn’t use OpenRouter’s Responses API. An agent that speaks Responses, such as Codex, is translated to one of the two above.

## Model list

- **Where it comes from..** magpie fetches the list from `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`, which gives each model’s context length. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from the `openrouter` catalog on models.dev.
- **Which models agents see..** OpenRouter lists hundreds. Unless you pick some, magpie shows agents the first 24 OpenRouter lists, newest first. Pick the rest in the provider’s model list, or turn on Best in family to keep only the newest of each family.
- **New models..** `auto-include` rules expose matching models now and each one a later fetch lists for the first time, and `refresh-every` has magpie fetch the list again by itself.
- **Image models..** OpenRouter’s `/models` lists text models only, so magpie reads image models such as FLUX, Seedream, Riverflow, Recraft and GPT Image from `/api/v1/images/models`. Choose one in Settings → Models → Images.
- **Decision models..** OpenRouter’s decision models (`liquid/d1`, `cloudflare/clef`, `~typesafe/jev-latest`…) are listed too, so a routing group can classify turns with the same key.

```
magpie provider models openrouter +anthropic/claude-opus-5.5   # expose one more
magpie provider models openrouter best                          # newest of each family
magpie provider auto-include openrouter '*:free'               # every free model, now and later
magpie provider refresh-every openrouter 1d
```

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
magpie codex openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
magpie gemini model openrouter/google/gemini-3-pro
magpie opencode openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does OpenRouter at `https://openrouter.ai/api`, so its requests are passed on as they are. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. magpie translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included: a Claude model goes to OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint, every other model to Chat Completions. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. magpie translates it the same way as Codex’s requests. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to OpenRouter as they are, except for Claude models, which magpie sends to the Anthropic endpoint for their prompt cache (see below). [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

If OpenRouter says a model isn’t served on the endpoint magpie chose, magpie builds the request again for the other one and remembers that for the model.

## Reasoning

- **Models that always reason..** Some OpenRouter models refuse to have reasoning turned off (“reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled”). When an agent asks for it off, magpie asks again with the level left to the model, on Chat Completions and on Messages alike.
- **Effort mid-conversation..** Claude Code sends a turn’s effort inside the conversation. OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint refuses that on some models, such as DeepSeek and GLM. magpie asks again at once without it, and doesn’t send it to OpenRouter again until magpie restarts.
- **Earlier thinking..** OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint turns away a thinking block without a signature, so magpie always sends one. On Chat Completions, earlier reasoning that an agent sends back in OpenRouter’s `reasoning` or `reasoning_details` fields is read as the model’s thinking.

## Cache, cost and credits

- **Claude’s prompt cache..** On Chat Completions, a relay that serves both APIs drops `cache_control`, and every turn is billed uncached. So magpie asks Claude models on OpenRouter’s Messages endpoint, from any agent, with the cache breakpoints the translation adds.
- **Cache tokens..** magpie reads cache reads and OpenRouter’s `cache_write_tokens` from each reply, so the Usage tab counts cache hits and writes apart from the rest.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call with OpenRouter’s prices from models.dev, or the model maker’s list price when the catalog has none. A model listed at $0, such as one ending in `:free`, shows free beside it in magpie’s pickers.
- **Which provider answered..** OpenRouter names the provider that served each reply. magpie keeps it, and the call’s details in the Usage tab show it as Upstream provider.
- **Credits..** The OpenRouter row shows what is left on the account, in dollars: total credits less total usage, read from `/api/v1/credits`. It’s the whole account’s figure, so each key of one account shows the same.

## Several keys and free models

One OpenRouter provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over. The provider’s routing can also rotate, weight or drain them instead. Adding the preset again makes a second OpenRouter provider; to spread requests over several keys, add them all to the one provider.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when OpenRouter is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.
- **Free models..** OpenRouter’s free models take 20 requests a minute. `rpm` holds each key to a rate: one request more waits for room, up to 2 minutes, then gets a 429 with a `Retry-After`.
- **Free-model 429s..** When a free model is refused by the shared pool of the provider serving it, magpie rests that model only and keeps the other free models in use. Any other 429 on a free model is OpenRouter’s account-wide free limit, and the key rests.
- **A pool of free models..** A routing group can take every free model OpenRouter lists with the pattern `openrouter/*:free`, today’s and those it lists later.

```
magpie provider rpm openrouter 20
magpie provider spend-cap openrouter <key> 20 month
magpie provider fallback openrouter deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
magpie group add my-free-pool models='openrouter/*:free' routing=order
magpie group set opus-anywhere stays=session models+=openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
```

## Troubleshooting

- **The model list has only `anthropic/` ids, or fails to load..** A provider given only `https://openrouter.ai/api` gets OpenRouter’s catalog under `anthropic/` names it doesn’t serve. Give it the Chat Completions base, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, or use the OpenRouter preset, which has both.
- **“Mid-conversation reasoning effort (configuration_update) is not supported”..** OpenRouter says this about Claude Code’s per-turn effort on models such as DeepSeek and GLM. magpie asks again at once without the effort, so the agent gets its answer, and stops sending it to OpenRouter until magpie restarts.
- **402 with “can only afford” or “fewer max_tokens”..** OpenRouter refused the request’s size or its in-flight budget, not because the balance is spent. magpie rests the key for half an hour and tries it again then; unlike a key out of credit, its rest doesn’t grow with each refusal.
- **Web search asks a model you didn’t pick..** It doesn’t: when OpenRouter answers magpie’s web search, magpie asks one of the OpenRouter models you have picked, since OpenRouter can refuse others for your region. For that search magpie turns on OpenRouter’s own `web` plugin, which works with any of its models.
- **Checking a key..** `magpie provider test openrouter` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use OpenRouter in Claude Code?

Add your OpenRouter key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, OpenRouter), then pick a model such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`. magpie writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and passes its requests on to OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint as they are.

### Can Codex use OpenRouter models?

Yes. Codex speaks only the Responses API, which magpie doesn’t use at OpenRouter. magpie translates each Codex request: a Claude model goes to OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint and every other model to Chat Completions, and the reply comes back to Codex as Responses.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use OpenRouter?

Yes. Gemini CLI’s requests are translated the same way as Codex’s. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to OpenRouter as they are, except for Claude models, which magpie sends to the Anthropic endpoint so the prompt cache works.

### How do I use only OpenRouter’s free models?

Make a routing group from the pattern `openrouter/*:free`, for example `magpie group add my-free-pool models='openrouter/*:free' routing=order`. It takes every free model OpenRouter lists, including ones it lists later. Models priced at $0 show free in magpie’s pickers.

### Why do OpenRouter’s free models answer 429?

OpenRouter’s free models take 20 requests a minute. Set `magpie provider rpm openrouter 20` and magpie holds requests back to that rate. When the 429 comes from the shared pool of the provider serving one free model, magpie rests only that model and keeps the other free models in use.

### Does magpie show my OpenRouter credits?

Yes. magpie reads OpenRouter’s credits endpoint and shows what is left in dollars: total credits less total usage. The figure is for the whole account, so every key of one account shows the same.

### Why does magpie fetch OpenRouter’s model list from /api/v1?

Asked at the Anthropic base, OpenRouter answers with its catalog under `anthropic/` names it doesn’t serve. magpie fetches the list from the Chat Completions base, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, and a provider given only OpenRouter’s Anthropic base is told to add that Chat base.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot

# GitHub Copilot in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

A Copilot seat comes with Claude, GPT and Gemini models, among others. Sign in to Copilot once in magpie, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use the models your plan gets, through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`. No API key.

## Sign in to Copilot

1. **Open Add provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider and click the Copilot tile.
2. **Enter the code on GitHub.** magpie shows a code and opens GitHub’s device page, `github.com/login/device`. Enter the code and approve. magpie then asks GitHub whose account it is and which plan it has, and the account shows under Copilot.
3. **Pick a model for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a `copilot/…` model.

```
magpie accounts add copilot                        # github.com
magpie accounts add copilot --host acme.ghe.com    # GitHub Enterprise on GHE.com
magpie accounts copilot                            # each account and what it has used
```

magpie serves a Copilot sign-in from three places:

- **Copilot’s editor plugins..** The sign-in they keep in `~/.config/github-copilot` (`apps.json` or `hosts.json`).
- **The Copilot CLI..** Its sign-in in `~/.copilot/config.json`, with the token in the system keychain or in that file. magpie on Windows also reads the Copilot CLI sign-in of a running WSL distro, from `config.json` only.
- **magpie’s own..** Each account you sign in with a code in magpie. Its token is kept in magpie’s own `logins.json`.

The editors’ and the CLI’s sign-ins are only read; magpie never writes them. When both are there, the editors’ github.com sign-in comes first, then the CLI’s, then an editor’s GHE.com sign-in. If GitHub turns away the editors’ token, magpie uses the CLI’s sign-in of the same account instead, never another account’s.

> **GitHub Enterprise on GHE.com.** An enterprise with data residency signs in at its own `<name>.ghe.com`, so add the account with `--host` (or answer the GHE.com question in the sign-in sheet). magpie accepts github.com or a `<name>.ghe.com` address and nothing else, so a GitHub token is never sent to a host of your choosing. The account is served at its enterprise’s `copilot-api.<name>.ghe.com`. One login on github.com and on GHE.com is two accounts: `you` and `you@acme.ghe.com`.

## The models your seat gets

magpie asks Copilot’s `/models` for each account and lists what comes back, so the list follows your plan rather than a fixed table. The models are named `copilot/` and Copilot’s own id: `copilot/claude-opus-5.5`, `copilot/gpt-5.4`, `copilot/gpt-5.3-codex`. `magpie models` prints them all.

- **Chat models only..** Copilot’s internal models and the ones no model picker offers are left out, and so is a model the account isn’t allowed to turn on.
- **Terms to accept..** A model whose terms are still waiting is listed anyway. The first request for it accepts them, as turning it on in Copilot’s editor would.
- **Reasoning efforts.** come from what Copilot lists for each model, and show in each agent’s picker.
- **Auto.** is always on the list; see Copilot Auto.
- **Image models.** such as GPT Image 2.5 Flare are listed for drawing (Settings → Models → Images), and are never offered as a chat model.
- **Older models..** A model for which Copilot names no API, such as GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o on a Student plan, is asked on Chat Completions only.

Claude Code reads a Claude version written with a dot as an older model, so magpie gives it Copilot’s Claude models with dashes (`claude-opus-5-5`) and turns the name back before the request reaches Copilot. Other agents see Copilot’s own spelling.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude copilot/claude-opus-5.5
magpie codex copilot/gpt-5.4
magpie gemini model copilot/gpt-5.4-mini
magpie opencode copilot/claude-opus-5.5
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Copilot serves its Claude models on Messages too, so Claude Code’s requests go to them as they are; a GPT or Gemini model gets them translated. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses, and magpie asks Copilot’s OpenAI models on Responses, so they pass through. Codex’s web search runs on Copilot’s side for those models, and Codex’s native compaction works with them too, but not with Copilot’s Claude models. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. magpie points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

The Copilot CLI is one of the agents magpie connects, too. Its row offers `auto` (Copilot picks) and Copilot’s own models, plus every other model you have added to magpie, which reach it through the Copilot CLI’s `providers.json`.

## How requests reach Copilot

Copilot doesn’t serve every model on every API. Its newest OpenAI models answer only on Responses; its Claude models on Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages; its Gemini models and the older ones on Chat Completions only. magpie sends each request on an API the model is served on, and translates between that API and the agent’s when they differ, streaming and tool calls included.

- **Wrong API..** When Copilot answers that a model isn’t served on the API it was asked on, magpie rebuilds the request for the next one and remembers which one worked.
- **Pin one yourself..** `magpie model api copilot/<model> chat` (or `responses`, `anthropic`) asks the model on that API only; `auto` hands the choice back to magpie.
- **Tool schemas for Gemini..** Copilot turned some of Codex’s tool schemas away for its Gemini models with 400 “invalid request body”. magpie rewrites the ones it can prove safe to rewrite, so those tools reach the model.

## Copilot Auto

`copilot/auto` is the model Copilot chooses for your account. It isn’t in Copilot’s `/models`, so magpie always adds it. On a Student plan it is the only model you may choose.

- magpie asks Copilot for a pick with the turn’s prompt, at Copilot Chat’s default setting, and keeps a pick for at most an hour.
- If Copilot has no Auto for the account, or picks a model the account was refused, a model the account may pick by hand stands in for 10 minutes: Copilot’s base model, its default, `gpt-4.1`, a model that isn’t premium, then the rest.
- If Copilot then refuses the model Auto picked, magpie picks another and sends the request again.
- The model Auto chose is noted on the request’s route, so you can see what answered.

## Premium requests, usage and cost

Each Copilot account has a card with three allowances, as GitHub reports them: Premium requests, Chat requests and Completions, each as used / allowance. `magpie accounts copilot` prints the same.

- **Monthly..** The allowances renew each month, on the date GitHub gives.
- **Unlimited.** shows as Unlimited. A window GitHub gives no figure for is left off the card, never shown as unlimited.
- **One request a turn..** A turn you type is billed as one request; the tool replies that carry it on are not.
- **Business and Enterprise..** A seat that uses up its allowance is paused, so magpie counts the account as used up and moves on to the next one. An organization’s pooled premium allowance shows as used up once the pool is spent.
- **Other plans..** When your plan lets you pay past the premium allowance, using it up doesn’t stop the account. Completions are counted too, but no request through magpie uses them.
- **No allowance..** Copilot’s base model, `gpt-4.1`, is billed to no allowance on any plan.

The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model that went through magpie. Cost on a subscription is an estimate at the model maker’s list price, or at the price you set for the model. One difference from Anthropic’s own pricing: Copilot bills a cache write at one price however long it is kept, so magpie prices a 1-hour write at the 5-minute rate. For `claude-opus-5.5` that is $5 per million tokens, where Anthropic’s 2× input would be $8.

## Several accounts and failover

- **Add another..** Click the Copilot tile again, or run `magpie accounts add copilot` again. The one in use is listed first, then the rest in the order you added them.
- **Choose which goes first..** `magpie accounts switch copilot <login>`; `magpie accounts forget copilot <login>` removes one. With the same login on github.com and GHE.com, name it in full (`you@acme.ghe.com`) or add `--host`.
- **Spread requests..** Tick the accounts to use on Copilot’s row. Routing sets how requests spread over them, Smart by default; the provider’s Fallback lists models to use when every account is out, rate limited or down. See [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions#accounts).
- **One model from two subscriptions..** Claude Opus from your Claude subscription and from Copilot become one group by themselves, `auto/<model>`. To set the order yourself: `magpie group add "Opus anywhere" models=claude/claude-opus-5-5,copilot/claude-opus-5.5 routing=order`.
- **A stale editor sign-in..** When GitHub refuses the token Copilot’s editors keep, an account you signed in to magpie with the same login is kept and used.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub refused this Copilot sign-in; sign in again | GitHub turned the account’s token away. Sign in again from its row: the account is signed in again in place, and its settings stay. A network error or a 5xx from GitHub never marks an account, and the mark goes when a request is served. |
| the GitHub token Copilot’s editors keep in … was refused | The editors’ sign-in has lapsed. Sign in to Copilot again in your editor or in magpie, or move that file aside. |
| <login> has no Copilot subscription | The GitHub account you approved has no Copilot plan. Sign in with the account that has the seat. |
| Copilot doesn’t serve this model on Anthropic’s Messages API; it isn’t about your plan | Copilot serves that model on other APIs only. `magpie model api copilot/<model> chat` sends it on Chat Completions. |
| The requested model is not supported. | Copilot won’t serve that model to this account now. magpie leaves it out of the account’s models and the agents’ pickers for 6 hours, then tries it again. Under Auto, another model is picked and the request is sent again. |
| Copilot doesn’t offer Auto to this account … | Copilot made no pick and the account lists no model it may pick by hand. Check the plan at `github.com/settings/copilot`. |
| the code expired; start again · the sign-in was declined on GitHub | The device code ran out before it was entered, or the request was declined on GitHub’s page. Start the sign-in again. |
| Copilot signs in on github.com or an enterprise’s <name>.ghe.com, not … | The `--host` given isn’t github.com or a GHE.com address. |
| subscription accounts are off in magpie | Settings → Privacy → Subscription accounts is off (or `magpie accounts discovery off` was run), so magpie reads no sign-in and serves no subscription, Copilot included. Turn it on, or run `magpie accounts discovery on`. |

## FAQ

### How do I use GitHub Copilot in Claude Code?

Sign in to Copilot in magpie (Providers, Add provider, Copilot; GitHub gives you a code to enter), then pick a `copilot/…` model such as `copilot/claude-opus-5.5` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude copilot/claude-opus-5.5`. magpie writes Claude Code’s `settings.json`. Copilot’s Claude models get Claude Code’s Anthropic requests as they are; its GPT and Gemini models get them translated.

### Can Codex use Copilot’s models?

Yes. Codex speaks OpenAI Responses, and magpie asks Copilot’s OpenAI models on Responses too, so they pass through, web search included. Copilot’s Claude and Gemini models are translated. Pick one on Codex’s row or run `magpie codex copilot/gpt-5.4`; it shows in Codex’s `/model` list.

### Can I use Copilot in Gemini CLI and OpenCode?

Yes. Run `magpie gemini model copilot/gpt-5.4-mini` or `magpie opencode copilot/claude-opus-5.5`, or pick the model on the agent’s row. magpie translates Gemini CLI’s requests, and writes the model into OpenCode’s `opencode.json`.

### Do I need VS Code or another editor signed in to Copilot?

No. magpie signs in to GitHub itself with a device code. If Copilot’s editor plugins or the Copilot CLI are already signed in on this computer, magpie reads that sign-in too, and never changes it.

### Does it spend my premium requests?

Requests go to Copilot on your account, so they count against your plan as Copilot counts them. A turn you type is billed as one request; the tool replies that carry it on are not. magpie shows each account’s Premium requests, Chat requests and Completions as used out of the allowance.

### Does it work with Copilot Business, Enterprise and GHE.com?

Yes. magpie reads the plan from GitHub: Free, Pro, Pro+, Max, Education, Business or Enterprise. An enterprise on GHE.com signs in with `magpie accounts add copilot --host <name>.ghe.com`. A Business or Enterprise seat that uses up its allowance is paused, and magpie counts the account as used up until it renews.

### Why is a Copilot model missing from my list?

magpie lists what Copilot’s `/models` gives the account: chat models only, without the ones no model picker offers or the account can’t turn on. A model Copilot answered with “The requested model is not supported.” is left out for 6 hours, then tried again in case your plan changed.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Copilot CLI on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot-cli). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

# Gemini in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Google serves Gemini on the Gemini Developer API, the one an AI Studio key opens, and on Vertex AI in your own Google Cloud project. Add either to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Gemini 3 models such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` through magpie’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent on a model of its own.

## Add a Gemini API key

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey).
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Google Gemini, paste the key and save. magpie asks Google which models it serves.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Gemini model such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`.

```
magpie provider add google AIza…
magpie provider test google
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so the Gemini API’s read `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`: the provider, then Google’s own id. The key is kept in magpie’s settings; magpie doesn’t take it from your shell.

## Endpoints

| API | Base URL | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions (OpenAI-compatible) | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | the model list, and requests from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other agents |
| Gemini API | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta` | Gemini CLI’s requests, Google Search, image models |

The preset fills in the Gemini API URL once. If you clear it, it stays empty. Every request that doesn’t come from a Gemini client goes to Chat Completions.

## Model list

- **Where it comes from..** magpie asks the OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the list once. It is the Gemini API’s list too, so magpie doesn’t ask twice. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from the `google` catalog on models.dev.
- **Image models..** At Google, a Gemini image model draws on the Gemini API. Choose one in Settings → Models → Images.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what magpie writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
magpie claude google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
magpie codex google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
magpie gemini model google/gemini-3.8-flash
magpie opencode google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. magpie translates each request to Gemini’s Chat Completions and the reply back to Messages, streaming and tool calls included. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. magpie translates it to Chat Completions the same way, and the reply comes back to Codex as Responses. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s own API, so its requests go to the Gemini API as it sends them, and its Google Search runs there. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Google as they are. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Thinking

- **Visible thoughts..** Gemini’s OpenAI-compatible API gives the model’s thoughts only when asked in `thinking_config`. When an agent asks for visible reasoning, magpie asks for the thoughts with `include_thoughts`, so a long think shows as thinking instead of a first word that comes late.
- **Levels and budgets..** Gemini 3 and later are sent a thinking level. Gemini 2 models are sent a budget instead: 1024 tokens for minimal and low, 8192 for medium and 24576 for high. xhigh and max are sent as high, and an effort with no level is left to the model.
- **Reasoning off..** Gemini 3 can’t stop thinking. When an agent turns reasoning off, magpie asks for the model’s lowest level instead.
- **A level the model doesn’t have..** Not every Gemini 3 has every level: `gemini-3.8-flash` has no minimal. When Google turns a level away with a 400, magpie asks again at the nearest level the model has and remembers it until magpie restarts.
- **`thinking_config` turned away..** That is a different 400: a server in front of Gemini that refuses the field itself. magpie asks again with `reasoning_effort` alone and stops sending `thinking_config` there.
- **Proxies..** A Gemini model behind a proxy on this computer or your network, such as one on `localhost` or a private address, is handled the same way.

## Thought signatures and tools

- **Thought signatures..** Gemini 3 signs the first function call of each step, and the next request fails with 400 “Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts” if the signature is gone. Agents don’t keep it. magpie carries it in the call id the agent gets, as a short reference to a file in magpie’s folder, and puts it back on the way to Gemini. Signatures are kept for 90 days.
- **Calls Gemini didn’t sign..** A call from another model earlier in the conversation, or one whose id an agent shortened, goes with Google’s documented `skip_thought_signature_validator`, so a conversation can move to Gemini halfway.
- **One provider’s signature..** A signature goes back only to the provider that gave it. In a routing group of Vertex AI and the Gemini API, the other provider gets the call as unsigned history instead of answering “Corrupted thought signature”.
- **Tool schemas..** magpie gives each untyped schema in an agent’s tools a type, which Vertex AI needs, and removes boolean schemas and `x-` keywords such as MCP’s `x-mcp-header`. Tools that need none of this go as they came.
- **The end of a stream..** Gemini’s OpenAI-compatible API sends a whole function call in one chunk and its `finish_reason` in the next. If that reason is lost after the usage arrived, magpie fills it in; without the usage, the reply is reported as cut off rather than passed on as complete.

## Cache, cost and search

- **Prompt cache..** Gemini keeps a prompt cached without saying so on that turn. magpie counts such a turn as a cache write and keeps the next turn on the same provider and key, and remembers which one answered across restarts.
- **Cached and thinking tokens..** magpie reads cached tokens and reasoning tokens from each reply, on Chat Completions and on the Gemini API alike, and the Usage tab counts them.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call from the `google` catalog on models.dev.
- **Web search..** Gemini runs Google Search on the Gemini API only for a request that declares no function tools. Claude Code’s and Codex’s requests declare tools, so their web search is magpie’s own, which the Google provider answers itself on your key: those searches spend your Gemini API credit.

## Several keys and rate limits

One Google Gemini provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over. The provider’s routing can also rotate, weight or drain them instead.

- **Per-minute 429s..** Gemini’s 429 “You exceeded your current quota … Please retry in 33s” for a per-minute limit is read as a rate limit, not a used-up plan, and so is Vertex AI’s `requests_per_minute_per_project`. The key rests from a minute, doubling, up to `rest-cap`.
- **Holding to a rate..** `rpm` holds each key to a number of requests a minute: one request more waits for room, up to 2 minutes, then gets a 429.
- **Out of quota..** `quota-rest` sets how long a key rests once its quota is spent: 15 minutes by default, up to 8 days, or until a time of day.
- **Spend caps and fallbacks..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, and `fallback` names where requests go when Gemini is out of quota or down.

```
magpie provider rpm google 10
magpie provider spend-cap google <key> 20 month
magpie provider fallback google google-vertex/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
```

## Vertex AI

The Google Vertex AI preset asks Gemini in your Google Cloud project, with no API key. Give it the project’s id; the project in each request is the one billed.

```
gcloud auth application-default login
magpie provider add google-vertex project=my-project
magpie claude google-vertex/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
```

- **Credentials..** magpie signs with gcloud’s Application Default Credentials, or with the file `credentials=` names by its full path: a user sign-in, a service account key or an impersonated service account. `impersonate=` takes a service account’s email, and needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on it. The metadata server, workload identity federation and Vertex AI’s express-mode API keys aren’t read.
- **Location..** `location=` is `global` (the default), `us`, `eu` or a region such as `us-central1`.
- **Models..** The preset has its own list, among them `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, partner models such as `zai-org/glm-5.2-maas`, and Claude models such as `claude-opus-5-5`. Gemini goes to Vertex AI’s Gemini API, a partner model to its OpenAI-compatible chat completions, and Claude to Anthropic’s Messages API, all in your project.
- **Thinking on Vertex AI..** A Gemini 3 level is fitted to the levels that model has, and reasoning off asks for its lowest. Gemini 2.5 takes a budget: Pro from 128 to 32768 tokens (128 when off), Flash up to 24576 (0 when off), Flash-Lite from 512 to 24576 (0 when off).

## Google sign-ins

Two Google sign-ins give Gemini models without a key. They are subscriptions, set up as on [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions).

- **Gemini (Code Assist)..** Gemini CLI’s Google sign-in, as `gemini/…`: `magpie accounts add gemini`. Google answers it only for a Code Assist Standard or Enterprise account with a Google Cloud project of its own; `magpie accounts project gemini <email> <project>` names the project.
- **Antigravity..** As `antigravity/…`: `magpie accounts add antigravity`. Its sign-in gives Antigravity’s Claude and Gemini models.

## Troubleshooting

- **“Thinking level MINIMAL is not supported for this model”..** The model has no minimal level. magpie asks again at the nearest level it has, so the agent gets its answer, and remembers the level until magpie restarts. Only when no level is left does the error reach the agent as Google sent it.
- **“Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts”..** A Gemini 3 call lost its signature. Through magpie the signature rides in the call id and is put back, and a call with none goes with `skip_thought_signature_validator`.
- **“Corrupted thought signature”..** The signature was cut short or came from another provider. magpie sends a signature only to the provider that gave it.
- **429 with “Please retry in 33s”..** A per-minute limit, not a spent plan. The key rests for a short while, and `rpm` keeps requests under the limit from then on.
- **Vertex AI: a schema “didn’t specify the schema type field”..** magpie types every untyped tool schema it sends to Gemini, so this shouldn’t reach the agent.
- **Vertex AI won’t save..** “Google Vertex AI needs the id of your Google Cloud project”: add `project=`. A credentials file has to be given by its full path.
- **Checking a key..** `magpie provider test google` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use Gemini in Claude Code?

Add a Gemini API key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, Google Gemini), then pick a model such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. magpie writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and translates each Messages request to Gemini’s Chat Completions, tool calls and streaming included.

### Can Codex use Gemini models?

Yes. Codex speaks only the Responses API. magpie translates each Codex request to Gemini’s Chat Completions and the reply back to Responses. Run `magpie codex google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, or pick the model on Codex’s row.

### Does Gemini 3 Pro keep working across tool calls in Claude Code?

Yes. Gemini 3 signs its function calls and refuses the next request without the signature. magpie carries each signature in the call id the agent gets and puts it back on the way to Gemini, so tool loops keep going, and a call from another model is sent as unsigned.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use my Gemini key through magpie?

Yes. Gemini CLI’s requests go to the Gemini API as it sends them, Google Search included. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Gemini’s OpenAI-compatible API as they are.

### Why does Gemini answer 429 with “Please retry in 33s”?

That is a per-minute limit, not a spent quota. magpie reads it as a rate limit and rests the key briefly. Run `magpie provider rpm google 10`, with your own limit, and magpie holds requests to that rate.

### Can I use Gemini through Vertex AI instead of an API key?

Yes. Add the Google Vertex AI preset with your project’s id, for example `magpie provider add google-vertex project=my-project`. magpie signs with gcloud’s Application Default Credentials or a credentials file, and your project is billed.

### Can I use my Gemini Code Assist or Antigravity sign-in instead?

Yes. Both are subscriptions: `magpie accounts add gemini` or `magpie accounts add antigravity`, then pick a `gemini/…` or `antigravity/…` model. Code Assist needs a Standard or Enterprise account with a Google Cloud project of its own.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). To run Google’s Antigravity app on other models, see [Antigravity on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/antigravity). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.
