Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok

# Grok in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

xAI serves its Grok models on three APIs at once: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. Add an xAI API key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Grok through magpie’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own.

## Add xAI

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [console.x.ai](https://console.x.ai).
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick xAI, paste the key and save. magpie asks xAI which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Grok model such as `grok-4.7`.

```
magpie provider add xai xai-…
magpie provider test xai
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so xAI’s read `xai/grok-4.7`: the provider, then xAI’s own id. The key is kept in magpie’s settings; magpie doesn’t take it from your shell.

## Endpoints

| API | Base URL | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api.x.ai/v1` | the model list, OpenCode’s requests, and every request magpie translates, Gemini CLI’s among them |
| Responses | `https://api.x.ai/v1` | Codex’s requests, and web search that xAI runs itself |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://api.x.ai` | Claude Code’s requests |

An agent whose API xAI serves is passed on to that API. When magpie has to translate, it uses Chat Completions: it keeps Responses first only for OpenAI’s own models at OpenAI, and Messages first only for Claude models, and Grok is neither.

## Model list

magpie fetches the list from xAI, at `https://api.x.ai/v1/models`, so agents see the models your key can use. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from models.dev’s `xai` catalog. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
magpie provider models xai +grok-4.7
magpie provider refresh-every xai 1d
```

## In each agent

```
magpie claude xai/grok-4.7
magpie codex xai/grok-4.7
magpie gemini model xai/grok-4.7
magpie opencode xai/grok-4.7
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does xAI at `https://api.x.ai`, so its requests go there as they are, with the fixes below. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which xAI serves at `https://api.x.ai/v1`, so its requests go there as they are too. If xAI turns away Codex’s custom tools (“unknown variant `custom`”), magpie translates that model’s Codex requests from then on and offers those tools as ordinary functions. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API, which xAI doesn’t serve. magpie translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back, streaming and tool calls included. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to xAI as they are. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

Grok Build, xAI’s own CLI, can take magpie’s models too: magpie adds them to `~/.grok/config.toml`, so they join its `/model` picker.

## What magpie fixes for xAI

xAI’s API turns away a few things that agents send. magpie changes them on the way, on requests it passes on and on those it translates alike, so the agent never sees these errors:

- **Tool patterns..** xAI reads a tool’s `pattern` with a different regex engine, so a pattern such as Claude Code’s `^[^\s[\]]+$` on Windows failed with “Schema validation failed: … is not a "regex"”. magpie escapes it so xAI reads it as JavaScript does.
- **Tool roots..** A tool whose parameters start with `anyOf`, `oneOf` or `allOf`, such as a Codex desktop automation tool, is folded into an object from the first request. xAI otherwise answers “tool parameter root must be an object type”.
- **Empty fields..** `"required": null` in a tool’s schema, and `"content": null` on a Codex reasoning item, are left out. xAI otherwise answers “/required: null is not of type "array"” or “Could not decode the compaction blob”.
- **System turns..** Claude Code’s system turns in the middle of a conversation are folded into the top-level system prompt. xAI otherwise answers “Invalid request content: Invalid message role.”
- **A tool choice with no tools..** A request that sets `tool_choice` but offers no tools, such as Codex’s compaction summary, goes without it. xAI otherwise answers “A tool_choice was set on the request but no tools were specified”.
- **Codex’s added tools..** xAI’s Responses API doesn’t know Codex’s `additional_tools` items, so magpie puts their tools in the request’s `tools`.
- **Whole numbers..** Grok writes whole numbers in tool-call arguments with a fraction, such as `2500.0`, which Codex’s whole-number fields refuse. magpie writes `2500`, in streamed replies too.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** The effort an agent asks for is fitted to the nearest level the model has, as the catalog lists them. A model whose levels aren’t known is asked as the agent asked.
- **Reasoning off..** When an agent whose requests magpie translates, such as Gemini CLI, turns reasoning off and the model lists `none` among its levels, magpie asks for none.
- **Switching models mid-conversation..** xAI reads only the sealed reasoning it wrote itself. When a Codex conversation moves to Grok from GPT or from another account, xAI answers “Could not decrypt the provided encrypted_content”. magpie asks again without those items at once, and leaves them out for the rest of that conversation.

## Web search

- **Codex..** xAI runs web search itself on its Responses API, so Codex’s `web_search` is done by xAI.
- **Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode..** xAI’s Messages and Chat Completions APIs don’t search, so magpie gives the model its own search tool, answered by the searcher chosen in Settings, or by one magpie picks when none is chosen.
- **xAI as the searcher..** Because xAI searches by itself, magpie can pick an xAI key to search for models that can’t.

## Cache, cost and usage

- **Cache tokens..** magpie reads the cached tokens xAI reports in each reply, so the Usage tab counts cache hits apart from the rest of the prompt.
- **Keeping the cache..** With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is worth keeping, 1,024 tokens or more, and still warm, read within the last five minutes, so a turn isn’t sent to a key with a cold cache.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each Grok call with xAI’s prices from models.dev.
- **Balance..** magpie reads no balance from xAI. Type it in yourself with `key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what magpie has priced the key’s calls at since.

## Several keys and failover

One xAI provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when xAI is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.
- **A request xAI can’t read..** When xAI answers 422 “Failed to deserialize the JSON body … unknown item type”, the request goes to the next member of the routing group, and the key isn’t rested for it.

```
magpie provider spend-cap xai <key> 20 month
magpie provider key-balance xai <key> 25
magpie provider fallback xai deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## Troubleshooting

- **“maximum prompt length is …”..** The conversation is longer than the model takes. magpie tells the agent so the way it understands, `context_length_exceeded` or Anthropic’s “prompt is too long”, so the agent compacts and tries again.
- **“Could not decrypt the provided encrypted_content”..** Codex moved to Grok mid-conversation with another vendor’s reasoning in it. magpie asks again without it; see Reasoning.
- **“unknown variant `custom`”..** xAI turned away Codex’s custom tools. magpie translates that model’s Codex requests from then on; the first refusal is the last.
- **Checking a key..** `magpie provider test xai` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use Grok in Claude Code?

Add your xAI API key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, xAI), then pick a Grok model such as `grok-4.7` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude xai/grok-4.7`. Claude Code’s requests go through magpie’s gateway to xAI’s Anthropic Messages endpoint, `https://api.x.ai`.

### Can Codex use Grok 4?

Yes. xAI serves the Responses API that Codex speaks, so `magpie codex xai/grok-4.7` sends Codex’s requests to `https://api.x.ai/v1` as they are, with what xAI would refuse fixed on the way: tool schemas, a tool choice with no tools, and whole numbers Grok writes as `2500.0`.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use Grok?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s API, so magpie translates its requests to xAI’s Chat Completions and the replies back. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to xAI as they are. Run `magpie gemini model xai/grok-4.7` or `magpie opencode xai/grok-4.7`.

### Does web search work with Grok?

Yes. Codex’s web search is run by xAI itself on its Responses API. For Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, magpie gives the model its own search tool, answered by the searcher chosen in Settings, or by one magpie picks.

### Why did Codex fail after switching from GPT to Grok mid-conversation?

xAI can’t read reasoning that another vendor sealed, and answers “Could not decrypt the provided encrypted_content”. magpie asks again without those items and leaves them out for the rest of the conversation.

### Does magpie show my xAI balance?

No. The Usage tab counts tokens, cache and cost for every Grok call, priced from models.dev, but magpie reads no balance from xAI. You can type the balance in with `magpie provider key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what magpie has priced since.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral

# Mistral in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Mistral serves its models on one API, OpenAI-style Chat Completions, at `api.mistral.ai`. Add a Mistral API key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Mistral through magpie’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own. Agents that speak another API are translated on the way.

## Add Mistral

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [console.mistral.ai](https://console.mistral.ai/api-keys). A Le Chat plan’s Vibe key goes in the same provider.
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Mistral, paste the key and save. magpie asks Mistral which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Mistral model such as `mistral-large-4`.

```
magpie provider add mistral <key>
magpie provider test mistral
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so Mistral’s read `mistral/mistral-large-4`: the provider, then Mistral’s own id. The key is kept in magpie’s settings; magpie doesn’t take it from your shell.

Already set Mistral up in OpenCode or Alma? magpie’s import from those apps brings it in as the Mistral provider. An app that keeps one entry per key (“Mistral #0001”, “Mistral #0002”…) becomes one Mistral provider with that many keys, listed once in every agent’s picker.

## Endpoints

| API | Address | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | the model list and every agent’s requests: OpenCode’s as they are, Claude Code’s, Codex’s and Gemini CLI’s translated |
| Billing | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/billing/budget`, `/v1/billing/subscription` | a key’s month of Vibe or API budget, and the plan it is on |

magpie’s Mistral provider has no Anthropic Messages or Responses address, so an agent that speaks either is translated to Chat Completions and the reply translated back, streaming and tool calls included.

## Model list

magpie fetches the list from Mistral, at `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/models`, so agents see the models your key can use. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from models.dev’s `mistral` catalog, and Devstral, Codestral and Magistral models carry Mistral’s logo in every picker. Mistral also serves models from other labs, such as GLM and DeepSeek’s `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`; they come through the same key, and the fixes below apply to them too. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
magpie provider models mistral +mistral-large-4 +mistral-medium-3.5
magpie provider refresh-every mistral 1d
```

## In each agent

```
magpie claude mistral/mistral-large-4
magpie codex mistral/mistral-large-4
magpie gemini model mistral/mistral-large-4
magpie opencode mistral/mistral-large-4
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which Mistral doesn’t serve. magpie translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back; a reasoning model’s thinking reaches Claude Code as thinking, then the text. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which Mistral doesn’t serve either, so its requests are translated too. Codex’s custom tools, such as `apply_patch`, are offered to the model as functions, and its calls come back as the custom tool calls Codex runs. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API. magpie translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Mistral as they are, with the fixes below. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## What magpie fixes for Mistral

Mistral’s API is strict about what it takes and sends a reasoning model’s thinking in a shape of its own. magpie changes both on the way, on requests it passes on and on those it translates alike:

- **Thinking in typed parts..** Mistral sends a reasoning model’s thinking as typed parts in `content`, thinking and text sometimes in one chunk, where the Chat contract has a string. OpenCode turned the first such chunk away (“Invalid … stream event”). magpie moves the thinking to `reasoning_content` and the text to a plain string, streamed or not.
- **Thinking sent back..** OpenCode sends an earlier turn’s thinking back in `reasoning_content`, which Mistral refuses with 422 `extra_forbidden`. magpie puts it in the thinking part Mistral itself returns, ahead of the turn’s text, so the thinking stays in context. Translated requests get the same, so a Codex tool loop keeps going on a DeepSeek model served by Mistral.
- **Fields Mistral doesn’t know..** OpenCode’s `store` and Kimi Code’s thinking switch got 422 `extra_forbidden`. magpie asks again without the optional fields Mistral named, and doesn’t send them to it again once that works.
- **Ollama options..** An agent that took the gateway for an Ollama server, such as Hermes Agent, sends Ollama’s `options` (its `num_ctx`) beside the Chat fields. magpie leaves them out, so Mistral never sees them.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** The effort an agent asks for is fitted to the nearest level the model has, as the catalog lists them. A model whose levels aren’t known is asked as the agent asked.
- **Reasoning off..** When an agent whose requests magpie translates, such as Gemini CLI, turns reasoning off and the model lists `none` among its levels, magpie asks for none.
- **Thinking across turns..** Each agent sees a reasoning model’s thinking in its own shape: `reasoning_content` for OpenCode, thinking blocks for Claude Code, reasoning for Codex. When it comes back in a later turn, Mistral gets it as a thinking part; see What magpie fixes.

## Web search

Mistral’s Chat Completions API doesn’t search the web for magpie, so magpie gives the model its own search tool in every agent, answered by the searcher chosen in Settings, or by one magpie picks when none is chosen.

## Vibe, cost and usage

- **Vibe month..** A Le Chat plan (Pro, Student or Team) comes with a month of Mistral Vibe. Its Vibe key’s row shows how much of the month’s budget is used, in the currency Mistral bills in, when it resets, and the plan’s name.
- **API month..** A Studio key made in the console shows the organization’s API budget, as “API · Month”, apart from a Vibe month. The budget is the organization’s, so every key of one organization shows the same numbers. A key with no budget has no card.
- **Pay as you go..** With pay-as-you-go on, what goes past the budget is billed rather than stopped, so a used-up month doesn’t stop the key’s models.
- **Cache tokens..** When a reply reports cached prompt tokens, the Usage tab counts them apart from the rest of the prompt.
- **Keeping the cache..** With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is worth keeping, 1,024 tokens or more, and still warm, read within the last five minutes.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call with Mistral’s prices from models.dev. magpie reads no balance from Mistral; type it in with `key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what magpie has priced the key’s calls at since.

## Several keys and failover

One Mistral provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when Mistral is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.

```
magpie provider spend-cap mistral <key> 20 month
magpie provider key-balance mistral <key> 25
magpie provider fallback mistral deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## Troubleshooting

- **422 `extra_forbidden`, “Extra inputs are not permitted”..** Mistral turned away a field it doesn’t know. magpie fixes the ones agents are known to send and asks again without an optional field Mistral names; see What magpie fixes.
- **“Invalid … stream event” in OpenCode..** That was Mistral’s thinking in typed parts. magpie sends OpenCode the thinking in `reasoning_content` and the text as a string.
- **No Vibe card..** magpie shows the month only for a key Mistral says is a Vibe key or a Studio key, and only when its budget is more than zero.
- **Checking a key..** `magpie provider test mistral` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use Mistral in Claude Code?

Add your Mistral API key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, Mistral), then pick a Mistral model such as `mistral-large-4` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude mistral/mistral-large-4`. Mistral serves Chat Completions only, so magpie translates Claude Code’s Anthropic Messages requests to `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` and the replies back, thinking included.

### Can Codex use Devstral and other Mistral models?

Yes. Codex can use any model your Mistral key lists, Devstral among them. Codex speaks OpenAI Responses, which Mistral doesn’t serve, so magpie translates each request to Chat Completions, offers Codex’s custom tools such as apply_patch as functions, and gives the calls back the way Codex runs them.

### How do I use Codestral or other Mistral models in OpenCode?

Pick the model in magpie, or run `magpie opencode mistral/mistral-large-4`; Codestral and Devstral work the same way when your key lists them. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Mistral as they are, with what Mistral would refuse fixed on the way: OpenCode’s `store` field, and earlier turns’ thinking sent back in `reasoning_content`.

### Can Gemini CLI use Mistral?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s Gemini API, so magpie translates its requests to Mistral’s Chat Completions and the replies back, streaming and tool calls included. Run `magpie gemini model mistral/mistral-large-4`.

### Why does Mistral answer 422 extra_forbidden?

Mistral turns away any field it doesn’t know. magpie sends an earlier turn’s thinking as the thinking part Mistral takes, leaves out Ollama options some agents add, and asks again without an optional field Mistral names, such as OpenCode’s `store`, then stops sending it.

### Does magpie show my Le Chat plan’s Vibe budget?

Yes. A Vibe key from a Le Chat plan (Pro, Student or Team) shows how much of the month’s Vibe budget is used, in the currency Mistral bills in, and when it resets, with the plan’s name. A Studio key made in the console shows the organization’s API budget instead, as “API · Month”.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama

# Ollama in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Ollama serves the models you pull on two APIs, OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages, at `http://localhost:11434`. Ollama Cloud serves its models the same way at `ollama.com`, with an API key. Add either to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use them through magpie’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own.

## Add Ollama

1. **Pull a model.** Pull a model in Ollama, such as `qwen3`, and leave the server running.
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider and pick Ollama under On this machine. No key is needed. magpie asks the server which models it has, and they show as `ollama/…`.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose an Ollama model.

```
ollama pull qwen3
magpie provider add ollama
magpie provider test ollama
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so a model you pulled as `qwen3` reads `ollama/qwen3`. A tag stays in the id, as in `ollama/qwen3:8b`. In the terminal UI, magpie asks for the server’s address when you add it. LM Studio, oMLX, vLLM and llama.cpp’s server are in [Local models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/local-models).

## Another port or another computer

If Ollama listens on another port, or runs on another computer such as a GPU box or a NAS, change Server address in the provider’s editor. Only the scheme, host and port change; each API keeps its path. The scheme can be left out, and `http` is taken; a path pasted with the address, such as `/v1`, is dropped.

```
magpie provider set ollama address=192.168.1.20:11434
magpie provider set ollama address=     # back to the default
```

- **Proxies..** A server on your own network is reached directly, whatever proxy Settings or the system name. A proxy you set on the provider itself is still used.
- **HTTPS..** An Ollama behind HTTPS with a self-signed certificate can be reached with Don't check its certificate in the editor. It applies to that provider’s own hosts only.

## Ollama Cloud

1. **Get a key.** Make one at [ollama.com/settings/keys](https://ollama.com/settings/keys).
2. **Add the provider.** In the Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Ollama Cloud, paste the key and save. magpie asks Ollama Cloud which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** Choose an Ollama Cloud model, such as `deepseek-v4-pro`, on the agent’s row.

```
magpie provider add ollama-cloud <key>
magpie claude ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4-pro
```

Names, reasoning levels and prices come from models.dev’s `ollama-cloud` catalog. The key is kept in magpie’s settings.

## Endpoints

| Provider | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ollama | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `http://localhost:11434` |
| Ollama Cloud | `https://ollama.com/v1` | `https://ollama.com` |

An agent whose API Ollama serves is passed on to that API. magpie uses no Responses endpoint for either, so when it has to translate, it uses Chat Completions: it keeps Responses first only for OpenAI’s own models, and Messages first only for Claude models.

## Model list

magpie asks the server for its list at the Chat Completions base: `http://localhost:11434/v1/models`, or `https://ollama.com/v1/models` for Ollama Cloud. A model shows in magpie once Ollama has it. After you pull another, press Fetch models in the provider’s editor, or run `magpie provider refresh ollama`. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
magpie provider refresh ollama
magpie provider models ollama +qwen3
```

Ollama 0.35.0 and later (0.40.5 for its cloud models) also serves decision models, such as Nimble, Clef and Tev. magpie reads Ollama’s `/api/tags` as well, and a model marked there as a decision model becomes one of the provider’s decision models for [intent routing](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/intent), never an agent’s model. An older Ollama lists none.

## In each agent

```
magpie claude ollama/qwen3
magpie codex ollama/qwen3
magpie gemini model ollama/qwen3
magpie opencode ollama/qwen3
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does Ollama at `http://localhost:11434`, so its requests go there as they are. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which magpie doesn’t send to Ollama. magpie turns each request into Chat Completions and the reply back, streaming and tool calls included. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API. magpie translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Ollama’s `/v1` as they are. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

Inside the agent, Claude Code’s and Codex’s `/model` list magpie’s models too, so you can move between a local model and a cloud one there. To go back to the agent’s own models, run `magpie claude default` or `magpie codex default`.

## Context window and num_ctx

Agents plan around how long a request the model takes. Claude Code takes a model it doesn’t know for 200K, and Codex compacts a conversation at 90% of the window it is told. magpie doesn’t read an Ollama chat model’s window, so tell it the real one: Context window under Advanced in the provider’s editor, for every model or one of them. magpie passes it on to the agents.

```
magpie provider set ollama context=32k
magpie provider set ollama context.qwen3=128k
```

- **`num_ctx`..** Some clients send Ollama’s per-request options, such as `{"num_ctx": …}`, beside the Chat Completions fields. magpie leaves them out of every request it sends on: no Chat Completions API reads them, Ollama’s own `/v1` included. The window the model runs with is Ollama’s to set; give magpie the same number.
- **Too long..** When a conversation outgrows the window, Ollama answers “exceeded max context length”. magpie tells the agent so the way it understands, `context_length_exceeded` or Anthropic’s “prompt is too long”, so the agent compacts and tries again.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** The effort an agent asks for is fitted to the nearest level the model has, as the catalog lists them. A model whose levels magpie doesn’t know is asked as the agent asked.
- **Reasoning off..** When an agent whose requests magpie translates, such as Codex or Gemini CLI, turns reasoning off and the model lists `none` among its levels, magpie asks for none.
- **Your own levels..** `magpie model efforts` offers only the levels you name, or sends a model no reasoning field at all.

```
magpie model efforts ollama/qwen3 low,medium,high
magpie model efforts ollama/qwen3 off
```

## Tool calls

Claude Code’s and OpenCode’s tool calls reach Ollama as the agent wrote them. For Codex and Gemini CLI, magpie translates the tools, the model’s calls and their results to Chat Completions and back, in streamed replies too.

## Privacy masking

magpie’s [privacy masking](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/masking) replaces keys, tokens and other secrets with placeholders before a request leaves the gateway, a request to a local Ollama too. When the model runs on your own computer or network, you can turn on Send requests unmasked in its editor, or run `magpie provider set ollama unmasked=yes`.

- **Cloud models..** Ollama’s cloud models pass a request on to a vendor whatever the address, so it is your call. The editor warns you while it is on for a provider that isn’t local, such as Ollama Cloud.
- **Tool arguments..** In a request in Ollama’s own format, a tool call’s arguments are masked as tool arguments, as in every other API.
- **Anonymous stats..** magpie’s daily stats name an Ollama model only when models.dev knows it; any other counts as “other”. See [Privacy](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/privacy).

## Usage and cost

- **Usage..** The Usage tab counts the tokens of every Ollama call. A model is priced at the price magpie finds for its id, which for a local model can be its maker’s list price. To count a local model at nothing, give it your own price.
- **Free first..** `free=yes` counts every model of the provider as free, so a Free first routing spends it before paid ones. Prices and Usage’s costs stay as listed.
- **Ollama Cloud’s allowance..** magpie reads the account’s balance from Ollama Cloud. The included allowance shows as a plan, in dollars used, with when it resets; an older plan shows its session and weekly limits instead. Credits you bought show as a balance. Past the allowance Ollama Cloud draws on those credits, so a spent allowance with credits left doesn’t stop the key.
- **Peak hours..** On Ollama Cloud, `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` (with their tags) cost double from 12:00 to 18:00 UTC, Monday to Friday. models.dev lists the off-peak price; the Usage tab doubles it in those hours, and a Cheapest first routing counts it.
- **Out of allowance..** When Ollama Cloud says a key is out without saying when it comes back, as its weekly limit does, magpie rests the key for 15 minutes. `quota-rest` sets how long, up to 8 days. With several keys (Add another key) the next one takes over; when every key is out, the gateway answers at once with Retry-After.

```
magpie model price ollama/qwen3 0,0,0,0
magpie provider set ollama free=yes
magpie provider quota-rest ollama-cloud 7d
magpie provider fallback ollama-cloud ollama/qwen3
```

## magpie as an Ollama server

Some apps take a custom model only as an Ollama server: VS Code’s Copilot Ollama provider, Visual Studio’s Copilot BYOK, Zed’s Ollama provider and the `ollama` CLI. Point them at magpie’s gateway, `http://127.0.0.1:3425`, and they see magpie’s models, from every provider, not only Ollama.

- **Routes..** magpie answers `/api/version`, `/api/tags`, `/api/show`, `/api/chat` and `/api/generate`.
- **The same path..** A chat there is served as `/v1/chat/completions` is, so key limits, routing, fallbacks and usage are the same. A gateway key held to some models lists only those.
- **What it tells..** `/api/tags` and `/api/show` mark tools, vision when the model reads images, and thinking when it reasons. `/api/show` also gives the model’s window, or 32768 for one magpie doesn’t know. The `ollama` CLI’s `name:latest` finds a model called `name`.

## Troubleshooting

- **A model you pulled isn’t listed..** The list comes from the server. Press Fetch models, or run `magpie provider refresh ollama`, and pick it in the provider’s model list. Use the name Ollama lists, tag included.
- **Ollama isn’t running..** `magpie provider test ollama` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name; add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would. Start Ollama, or check Server address. `fallback` names where requests go while it is down.
- **“exceeded max context length”..** The conversation is longer than the model was loaded for. Set the real Context window on the provider, and the agents compact before they reach it.
- **Another computer can’t be reached..** Check the address and port in Server address; for HTTPS with a self-signed certificate, turn on Don't check its certificate.

## FAQ

### How do I use Ollama in Claude Code?

Add Ollama in magpie (Providers, Add provider, Ollama under On this machine), then pick one of its models on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude ollama/qwen3`. Claude Code’s requests go through magpie’s gateway to Ollama’s Anthropic Messages API at `http://localhost:11434` as they are.

### Can Codex use Ollama?

Yes. Codex speaks only the Responses API, so magpie turns its requests into Chat Completions for Ollama, and the replies back, tool calls included. Run `magpie codex ollama/qwen3`.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use Ollama?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s API, so magpie translates its requests to Ollama’s Chat Completions and the replies back. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Ollama as they are. Run `magpie gemini model ollama/qwen3` or `magpie opencode ollama/qwen3`.

### How do I run qwen3-coder from Ollama in Claude Code?

Pull it in Ollama, press Fetch models in the provider’s editor in magpie (or run `magpie provider refresh ollama`), and pick it on Claude Code’s row. Its id in magpie is `ollama/` and the name Ollama lists it under, tag included. Set its Context window too: Claude Code takes a model it doesn’t know for 200K.

### Can magpie use Ollama on another computer?

Yes. Set the provider’s Server address to that computer, such as `magpie provider set ollama address=192.168.1.20:11434`. A server on your own network is reached directly, not through a proxy set in Settings or the system.

### Does magpie work with Ollama Cloud?

Yes. Add Ollama Cloud with a key from `ollama.com/settings/keys`. magpie lists the models the key can use, prices them from models.dev, and shows the account’s included allowance and the credits you bought.

### Do I need an API key for a local Ollama?

No. The Ollama preset takes none. Ollama Cloud needs one.

Other local servers, such as LM Studio, oMLX, vLLM and llama.cpp’s server, are in [Local models](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/local-models). To let a local model classify each request for routing, see [Intent routing](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/intent).

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

# Anthropic in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Anthropic serves Claude on its Messages API, at `api.anthropic.com`. Add an Anthropic API key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Claude models through magpie’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own. Agents that speak another API are translated on the way.

## Add Anthropic

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys). An API key starts with `sk-ant-api`.
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Anthropic, paste the key and save. magpie asks Anthropic which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Claude model such as `claude-opus-5-5`.

```
magpie provider add anthropic <key>
magpie provider test anthropic
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so Anthropic’s read `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`: the provider, then Anthropic’s own id. The key is kept in magpie’s settings; magpie doesn’t take it from your shell.

Already set Anthropic up in OpenCode or Alma? magpie’s import from those apps brings it in as the Anthropic provider.

This page is about an API key. A Claude Pro or Max subscription is signed in to separately; see [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions).

## Endpoints

| API | Address | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Messages | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` | every agent’s requests: Claude Code’s as sent, Codex’s, Gemini CLI’s and OpenCode’s translated |
| Models | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models` | the model list |

magpie’s Anthropic provider has no Chat Completions or Responses address, so an agent that speaks either, or Google’s Gemini API, is translated to Messages and the reply translated back, streaming and tool calls included.

## Model list

magpie fetches the list from Anthropic, at `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models`, every page of it, so agents see the models your key can use. Names, context windows and prices come from models.dev’s `anthropic` catalog. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
magpie provider models anthropic +claude-opus-5-5 +claude-sonnet-5-5 +claude-haiku-5-5
magpie provider refresh-every anthropic 1d
```

Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 take 1M tokens. On a window that long, Codex compacts a conversation at 272K rather than send ever more of it on every turn; `magpie model compact off` lets it run to the whole window. In Claude Code a Claude model runs to its own window, as Anthropic runs it: 200K unless a `[1m]` one is picked.

## In each agent

```
magpie claude anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
magpie codex anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
magpie gemini model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
magpie opencode anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, so its requests go to Anthropic as Claude Code sent them, its own cache marks, thinking and betas included, with the fixes below. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which Anthropic doesn’t serve. magpie translates each request to Messages and the reply back, marks the prompt for Anthropic’s cache, and keeps Claude’s signed thinking across a tool loop. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API. magpie translates each request to Messages and the reply back. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions to magpie, so its requests are translated to Messages too. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## What magpie does for Anthropic

A request magpie translates is built the way Anthropic’s Messages API wants it, and a few things Anthropic would refuse are fixed on Claude Code’s requests too:

- **Prompt caching..** Anthropic caches a prompt only up to a block marked with `cache_control`, and a request from another API has no marks. magpie marks the system prompt (or the last tool, when there is no system prompt) and the conversation’s last block, two marks at most, so the next turn reads what came before from the cache. A request that brings `cache_control` of its own keeps its marks, and magpie adds none.
- **An hour’s cache for Codex..** Codex’s turns are often more than five minutes apart, so the marks magpie adds to its requests last an hour, unless Codex asks `prompt_cache_retention` `in_memory`. An upstream that turns the hour’s `ttl` away is asked again with five-minute marks, and magpie remembers it.
- **Signed thinking..** Claude signs its thinking and wants it back on a tool loop’s next turn. Codex gets each thinking block, signature included, in its reasoning item’s `encrypted_content`, and magpie sends it back to Anthropic as it was; redacted thinking goes back sealed. Thinking with no signature is left out, and so is thinking another vendor signed, such as DeepSeek’s earlier in a routing group, which Claude refuses.
- **Tool calls..** A call an interrupted turn left unanswered gets a result saying it is unavailable, and a result for a call Anthropic never saw becomes text, where Anthropic would refuse the request. A history with calls but no tools declared declares them, with `tool_choice` none. A required tool goes as `any`, a named one as `tool`, and parallel calls turned off as `disable_parallel_tool_use`.
- **Sampling..** Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5 refuse `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k`, which Claude Code’s auto mode classifier sends. magpie leaves them out for those models.
- **Betas..** The betas an agent asks in `anthropic-beta` go on to Anthropic, save Claude Code’s own sign-in beta (`oauth-…`), which names a credential that never leaves magpie.
- **Structured output..** A request for JSON in a schema goes to Anthropic as `output_config.format`.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** Claude models from 4.6 on think adaptively. A translated request’s effort goes as `output_config.effort`, with thinking adaptive and its summary shown (`display: summarized`), since Opus 4.7 and later leave the thinking text out unless asked. Opus and Sonnet 4.6 have no xhigh, so xhigh is asked as max.
- **Budgets..** Older Claude models get a thinking budget: 4,096 tokens at low, 10,000 at medium, 24,000 at high, 32,000 at xhigh and max, fitted under the request’s `max_tokens`.
- **A budget to a newer model..** A request with a thinking budget to a model from 4.6 on, which Claude Opus 5.5 refuses (“requires adaptive thinking”), goes as adaptive thinking, the budget asked as the nearest effort.
- **Reasoning off..** Codex’s or a Chat client’s effort none turns thinking off, not down to a low budget. Each model takes off its own way: Sonnet 5.5 is sent `between_tools`, an effort above high asked as high; Opus 5.5 and Fable 5 always think, so thinking is left out; Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5 are asked high in place of xhigh or max; older Claudes take it as sent. Claude Code’s requests with thinking off are fitted the same way.

## Web search

Anthropic searches the web itself. Claude Code’s WebSearch goes to Anthropic as it is. When Codex, Gemini CLI or a Chat client asks to search, magpie offers Claude Anthropic’s own `web_search_20250305` tool, up to five searches a request, rather than magpie’s searcher.

## Cost and usage

- **Cache tokens..** The Usage tab counts cache reads, five-minute cache writes and hour-long cache writes apart from the rest of the prompt, as Anthropic reports them.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call with Anthropic’s prices from models.dev. An hour-long write is priced at twice the input price where the catalog gives none, as Anthropic bills it. magpie reads no balance from Anthropic; type it in with `key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what magpie has priced the key’s calls at since.
- **Keeping the cache..** With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is worth keeping, 1,024 tokens or more, and still warm: read within the last five minutes, or within the hour when it was written for an hour.

## Several keys and failover

One Anthropic provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when Anthropic is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.
- **Workspaces..** A key that reaches several workspaces names the one each request is for with the `anthropic-workspace-id` header. Add the provider again under an id of its own, with the header set in its Headers field or from the terminal; its models then read `anthropic-ws2/…`.

```
magpie provider spend-cap anthropic <key> 20 month
magpie provider key-balance anthropic <key> 25
magpie provider fallback anthropic deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
magpie provider add anthropic <key> id=anthropic-ws2 name="Anthropic WS2" header.anthropic-workspace-id=wrkspc_…
```

## Troubleshooting

- **“requires adaptive thinking”..** A thinking budget sent to a model from 4.6 on. magpie sends it as adaptive thinking with the nearest effort; see Reasoning.
- **400 when thinking is turned off..** Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5 each refuse `disabled`, and Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5 refuse it at xhigh and max. magpie sends each model off the way it takes it.
- **“`temperature` is deprecated for this model”..** magpie leaves `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` out for the models that refuse them.
- **“`tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks”..** An interrupted turn left a call unanswered. In a request magpie translates, the call gets a result saying it is unavailable.
- **“Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block”..** The conversation ran on another vendor first. magpie leaves thinking another vendor signed, or left unsigned, out of what goes to Claude.
- **A 400 about `cache_control` and `ttl`..** The upstream doesn’t take the hour-long marks magpie adds for Codex. magpie asks again with five-minute marks and keeps to them for that provider.
- **“this is an Anthropic API key, not a setup-token”..** The key went to the Claude subscription’s sign-in. Add it as the Anthropic provider instead.
- **Checking a key..** `magpie provider test anthropic` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use an Anthropic API key in Claude Code?

Add your Anthropic API key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, Anthropic), then pick a Claude model such as `claude-opus-5-5` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. Claude Code speaks Anthropic Messages, so its requests go to `https://api.anthropic.com` as it sent them, with what the model would refuse fixed on the way.

### Can Codex use Claude models?

Yes. Codex speaks OpenAI Responses, which Anthropic doesn’t serve, so magpie translates each request to the Messages API and the reply back. It marks the prompt for Anthropic’s cache with marks that last an hour, and keeps Claude’s signed thinking across a tool loop in Codex’s `encrypted_content`. Run `magpie codex anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.

### How do I use Claude in OpenCode through magpie?

Pick the model in magpie, or run `magpie opencode anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions to magpie, so magpie translates its requests to Anthropic’s Messages API, marks the prompt for the cache and fits the reasoning effort to the model.

### Can Gemini CLI use Claude?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s Gemini API, so magpie translates its requests to Anthropic’s Messages API and the replies back, streaming and tool calls included. Run `magpie gemini model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`.

### Does magpie keep Anthropic’s prompt cache for agents it translates?

Yes. A request from Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode has no cache marks of its own, so magpie marks the system prompt and the conversation’s last block, two marks at most, and the next turn reads what came before from the cache. A request that brings its own `cache_control` keeps its marks. Codex’s marks last an hour, the rest five minutes.

### Why does Claude answer 400 when thinking is turned off?

Newer Claude models don’t all take `thinking` `disabled`. magpie sends Sonnet 5.5 `between_tools`, leaves thinking out for Opus 5.5 and Fable 5, which always think, and asks Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5 at high in place of xhigh or max. Older Claudes get it as sent.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [OpenAI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) if you get stuck.

# OpenAI in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

OpenAI serves its models on two APIs at `api.openai.com`: Responses and Chat Completions. Its own models are best asked on Responses, and its newest answer only there. Add an OpenAI API key to magpie once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use OpenAI’s models through magpie’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own. Codex’s requests go to OpenAI as they are; the other agents’ are translated on the way.

This page is about an API key from platform.openai.com. A ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription is signed in to separately; see [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions).

## Add OpenAI

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys). It starts with `sk-`.
2. **Add the provider.** In magpie’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick OpenAI, paste the key and save. magpie asks OpenAI which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose an OpenAI model such as `gpt-6.1-sol`.

```
magpie provider add openai <key>
magpie provider test openai
```

Model ids in magpie are `provider/model`, so OpenAI’s read `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`: the provider, then OpenAI’s own id. The key is kept in magpie’s settings; magpie doesn’t take it from your shell.

Already set OpenAI up in OpenCode or another app magpie imports from? The import brings it in as the OpenAI provider.

## Endpoints

| API | Address | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Responses | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | OpenAI’s own models, ids starting `gpt-`, `codex` or `o` and a digit: Codex’s requests as they are, Claude Code’s, Gemini CLI’s and OpenCode’s translated |
| Chat Completions | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | the model list, and any other model the key lists |

magpie’s OpenAI provider has no Anthropic Messages address, so Claude Code’s requests are always translated. For OpenAI’s own models magpie keeps Responses first even for an agent that speaks Chat Completions. When OpenAI answers that a model is served only on `/v1/responses`, magpie asks again there and remembers it. To send a model on one API yourself:

```
magpie model api openai/gpt-5.5 chat
magpie model api openai/gpt-5.5 --reset
magpie model apis openai
```

**Azure OpenAI** is a provider of its own, Azure OpenAI. Give it your resource’s endpoint, `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com`, and its key. magpie uses the v1 API under `/openai/v1` for Chat Completions and Responses, sends the key in the `api-key` header, and lists the resource’s deployments as its models. A deployment named for its model, such as `gpt-5-codex`, goes to Responses first too.

## Model list

magpie fetches the list from OpenAI, at `https://api.openai.com/v1/models`, so agents see the models your key can use. Names, context windows, reasoning levels and prices come from models.dev’s `openai` catalog. A reasoning model OpenAI has just listed, before its levels are known, gets those of the newest reasoning model in its family: `gpt-6.1-sol` got `gpt-6-sol`’s. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
magpie provider models openai +gpt-6.1-sol +gpt-6-luna +gpt-5.5
magpie provider refresh-every openai 1d
```

## In each agent

```
magpie claude openai/gpt-6.1-sol
magpie codex openai/gpt-6.1-sol
magpie gemini model openai/gpt-6.1-sol
magpie opencode openai/gpt-6.1-sol
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which OpenAI doesn’t serve. magpie translates each request to Responses and the reply back; the model’s reasoning summary reaches Claude Code as thinking, then the text. [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks Responses, so its requests go to OpenAI as they are: its custom tools such as `apply_patch`, its reasoning items and its own `prompt_cache_key` included. Codex is also offered Fast here; see Reasoning. [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API. magpie translates each request to Responses and the reply back. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions. OpenAI’s own models go to Responses first, so magpie translates its requests there and the replies back; any other model the key lists gets OpenCode’s requests as they are. [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## What magpie does for OpenAI

- **A prompt cache key..** A translated request to OpenAI that carries no `prompt_cache_key` gets one, made from the session the agent names, or else its first user message, and hashed, so it names nothing of the agent. Codex sends its own, which goes on as it is, and one you set yourself wins. If OpenAI answers 400 over the field, magpie asks again without it.
- **Tools loaded where they were loaded..** A tool that Claude Code’s tool search loads mid-conversation is sent to OpenAI’s Responses API as an `additional_tools` item at that point, not added to the tool list, which keeps the cached prefix. `additional-tools=off` puts it with the other tools.
- **Sealed reasoning from elsewhere..** OpenAI reads only its own sealed reasoning (`encrypted_content`). An item sealed under another key, organization or account is refused (“could not be verified”); magpie asks again without those items and remembers it for the conversation. Claude’s thinking, which Codex carries in a reasoning item after a turn on a Claude model, is taken out before the request reaches OpenAI.
- **Earlier responses..** A Responses client may send only a turn’s new input and name the response it follows (`previous_response_id`). magpie keeps each response it gave such a client, in memory and under the caller’s gateway key. OpenAI keeps responses too, so when the same key answered the one named, OpenAI is sent only the new input after its own id. Codex over HTTP says `store` false and names none.
- **Codex’s own compaction..** With `compaction=native`, Codex’s compaction is asked of OpenAI as Codex sent it and the sealed item comes back to Codex as it came. Only the key that sealed it can read it, so later requests carrying it go only there. The default, `compaction=magpie`, has magpie summarise.

```
magpie provider set openai compaction=native
magpie provider set openai additional-tools=off
```

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** The effort an agent asks for is fitted to the nearest level the model has, as the catalog lists them: `gpt-6-sol` has `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`. On Responses it is sent as `reasoning.effort`, with `summary` set to `auto`, so the model’s reasoning summary comes back.
- **Reasoning off..** When an agent whose requests magpie translates, such as Gemini CLI, turns reasoning off and the model lists `none` among its levels, magpie asks for none.
- **Encrypted reasoning..** magpie passes on what an agent asks to include, but asks for `reasoning.encrypted_content` only with reasoning: OpenAI refuses it of a model that doesn’t reason. Codex sends the sealed items back on the next turn, and magpie passes them on as they are.
- **Fast..** On an OpenAI key, Codex is offered Fast for GPT and o-series models. magpie sends it as `service_tier: "priority"`, OpenAI’s priority processing. A service tier set for Codex in magpie overrides what Codex asked.

## Web search

OpenAI’s Responses API searches the web itself. When an agent offers its model web search, as Codex and Claude Code do, magpie gives the model OpenAI’s own `web_search` tool on Responses, and OpenAI runs the search.

## Cost and usage

- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call with OpenAI’s prices from models.dev.
- **Cache tokens..** When a reply reports cached prompt tokens, the Usage tab counts them apart from the rest of the prompt.
- **Keeping the cache..** With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is worth keeping, 1,024 tokens or more, and still warm, read within the last five minutes.
- **Service tier..** Each call records the tier the agent asked for, the one magpie sent, and the one OpenAI’s reply says it ran at.
- **Balance..** magpie reads no balance from OpenAI; type it in with `key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what magpie has priced the key’s calls at since.

## Several keys and failover

One OpenAI provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over. To keep keys apart instead, say from two organizations, add the provider again: the second is `openai-2`.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when OpenAI is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.

```
magpie provider spend-cap openai <key> 20 month
magpie provider key-balance openai <key> 25
magpie provider fallback openai deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## Troubleshooting

- **“The encrypted content for item rs_… could not be verified”..** The conversation carries reasoning sealed under another key, organization or account. magpie asks again without those items; see What magpie does.
- **A model that answers only on `/v1/responses`..** magpie moves it to Responses and remembers it. `magpie model apis openai` shows which API each model is asked on.
- **A 400 over `prompt_cache_key`..** magpie asks again without the key it added.
- **Checking a key..** `magpie provider test openai` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use OpenAI’s models in Claude Code?

Add your OpenAI API key in magpie (Providers, Add provider, OpenAI), then pick a model such as `gpt-6.1-sol` on Claude Code’s row, or run `magpie claude openai/gpt-6.1-sol`. OpenAI serves no Anthropic Messages API, so magpie translates Claude Code’s requests to OpenAI’s Responses API at `https://api.openai.com/v1` and the replies back, the reasoning summary as thinking.

### Can Codex use an OpenAI API key instead of a ChatGPT sign-in?

Yes. Add the key, then run `magpie codex openai/gpt-6.1-sol`. Codex speaks Responses, so its requests go to OpenAI as they are, custom tools and reasoning included, and Fast is sent as priority processing. A ChatGPT Plus or Pro sign-in is set up separately, in Subscriptions.

### How do I use GPT models in OpenCode?

Pick the model in magpie, or run `magpie opencode openai/gpt-6.1-sol`. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, but OpenAI’s own models go to Responses first, so magpie translates OpenCode’s requests there and the replies back. To send a model on Chat Completions instead, run `magpie model api openai/gpt-5.5 chat`.

### Can Gemini CLI use OpenAI?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s Gemini API, so magpie translates its requests to OpenAI’s Responses API and the replies back, streaming and tool calls included. Run `magpie gemini model openai/gpt-6.1-sol`.

### Does magpie keep OpenAI’s prompt cache?

Yes. Codex’s own `prompt_cache_key` goes on as it is. A translated request without one gets a key made from its session or first user message, hashed so it names nothing of the agent. With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is warm.

### Why does OpenAI say the encrypted content could not be verified?

OpenAI reads only reasoning it sealed for the same key, organization or account. When a conversation carries reasoning sealed elsewhere, magpie asks again without those items and remembers it for the conversation.

### Does magpie support Azure OpenAI?

Yes, as its own provider, Azure OpenAI. Give it the resource’s endpoint and key; magpie uses the v1 API under `/openai/v1`, sends the key in the `api-key` header and lists the resource’s deployments as models.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/anthropic) · [Gemini](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/ollama)
