Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in magpie and pick a GPT model under magpie on Pi’s row. pi sends its requests to magpie, which uses the subscription on the Responses API.

### Where does magpie write if I set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR?

In that folder, with ~ expanded. A relative path is ignored, and magpie uses ~/.pi/agent.

### Does it work with Pi in WSL?

Yes. magpie sets up a Pi in a WSL distro too, its provider pointing at the gateway as the distro reaches it.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Kimi Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi-code) and [Cursor Private Inference on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference

# Cursor Private Inference on any model

Cursor Private Inference is a build of Cursor whose agent runs on your own machine and asks a model endpoint of yours instead of Cursor’s backend. magpie is such an endpoint, so its agent can run on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

The build takes its endpoint from `CURSOR_LOCAL_AGENT_BASE_URL` and `CURSOR_LOCAL_AGENT_API_KEY`. magpie sets the two for your user, to the gateway’s `/v1` and a key of its own: through launchctl on the Mac, the registry’s Environment on Windows and environment.d on Linux. So the app has them when you open it from the Dock or the Start menu. magpie writes none of Cursor’s files, since regular Cursor shares them, and only this build reads the two variables. magpie finds the build by its `product.json`, in your apps folders, and on Linux as its AppImage where you downloaded it.

## Connect it

1. **Add providers in magpie.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick magpie on its row.** In the Agents tab, set Cursor Private Inference’s provider to magpie.
3. **Quit it and open it again.** Quit the app, not only its window, then open it. magpie’s models are in its model picker.

To start it from a shell instead, the row gives the command that starts it with both variables set.

## Its models

Its model picker lists the gateway’s models, the ones its key is shown. The row’s Models button picks which. For each model the gateway also says which APIs it is served on and its limits, so the build asks Claude on Anthropic Messages, GPT on Responses and the rest on Chat, with the right context.

## Effort

Neither the build’s environment nor, for most models, its app says how hard a model should reason. Pick the effort on the row instead, among the levels its models have, and the gateway asks each request for it. Left on the default, requests go as the app sends them.

## When it takes effect

The build keeps the model list it was first given until it quits, so quit it and open it again after a change. On the Mac, launchctl’s variables are gone after a restart: magpie sets them again when it starts, with the gateway’s address then, and the app takes them the next time it opens.

## Settings that come first

A base URL or API key set in the build’s Open configuration dialog, or in a model’s own settings, comes before the variables. Leave both empty, or set them to the gateway’s `/v1` address and the key the row shows.

## Switch back

Take the row off magpie. magpie clears both variables for your user. Quit the app and open it again.

## FAQ

### Can Cursor’s agent run on DeepSeek or GLM?

Yes, in Cursor Private Inference. Any model you have in magpie can be in its model picker: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Does it change my regular Cursor?

No. magpie writes none of Cursor’s settings. It sets two variables that only the Private Inference build reads.

### Why don’t the new models show?

The build keeps its first model list until it quits. Quit the app itself, not only its window, and open it again. Check that no base URL or key is set in its Open configuration.

### Does it work on Windows and Linux?

Yes. magpie sets the variables in the registry’s Environment on Windows and in environment.d on Linux, and finds the Linux AppImage where you downloaded it.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Pi on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/pi) and [Antigravity on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/antigravity). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/antigravity

# Antigravity on any model

Antigravity, Google’s agent app, can send its requests to a gateway of yours instead of Google, through its Enterprise Gateway setting. magpie is such a gateway, so Antigravity and its CLI, `agy`, can run on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

Antigravity 2.15 and later reads a `gateway` block from its settings file: `~/.antigravity/settings.json` up to 2.29, `~/.gemini/config/config.json` from 2.30. magpie writes that block, turned on, with its gateway’s address, a key that names the app and the `openai` wire protocol, and sets `models.defaultModelId` to the model you pick. The app then lists the gateway’s models in its picker and sends its chats to magpie, which translates each one for the model’s provider. Your own gateway, default model, model list and catalog are kept aside and put back when magpie steps out.

## Connect the app

1. **Add providers in magpie.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Antigravity’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under magpie.
3. **Restart Antigravity.** It reads its gateway at start-up. magpie’s models are then in its model picker.

```
magpie antigravity deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # the app on DeepSeek
magpie agy deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro            # agy on DeepSeek
```

## Its models

The picker lists the gateway’s models, the ones the app’s key is shown, under the names magpie’s catalog gives them. On its own the app gives every model it doesn’t know a 200K window. magpie points its `models.listSource` at the gateway’s catalog, which gives each model its real context window, so long sessions compact when they should.

## Effort

The catalog lists a model at each of its reasoning levels, so the app’s own picker offers them, and the level picked there goes with the request. The effort on magpie’s row is the level the app starts on, and what a model with no levels in the picker is asked for. Left on the default, requests go as the app sends them.

## Your Google sign-in

On a gateway, Antigravity uses no Google sign-in and its backend asks Google for nothing. What Google turns on for your account, its experiments and commands such as `/boost`, `/teamwork`, `/plugin` and `/generative_ui`, is gone while it is on magpie. Taking the row off magpie gives it back.

## The agy CLI

`agy` follows the app’s gateway unless it is connected on its own row. Connected there, it runs on magpie through the Gemini API: magpie keeps its models in `magpie-settings.json`, beside agy’s own `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, and starts agy with that file, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `--model` for that session. So that typing `agy` just works, magpie adds a function named `agy` to each shell’s profile while agy is on one of its models. A terminal opened before takes the command from the row. Your `settings.json` stays yours, so `agy remote-control` still runs on your Google sign-in.

## Settings that come first

An `admin_settings.json` your organisation installs, and the `AGY_LLM_GATEWAY_*` variables, win over the settings file field by field. If either sets a gateway of its own, Antigravity doesn’t reach magpie, and the row says so.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own models on the row, or take the row off magpie. magpie puts back your own gateway, default model, model list and catalog. For agy, it removes the shell function too. Restart Antigravity.

## FAQ

### Can Antigravity run on models other than Gemini?

Yes. Any model you have in magpie is in its picker: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Do I still need to sign in with Google?

No. On a gateway Antigravity uses no Google sign-in. What Google turns on for your account, such as /boost and /teamwork, is off while it is on magpie.

### Why does every model show a 200K context?

That is the app’s default for models it doesn’t know. magpie points its catalog at the gateway, which gives each model its real window. Restart Antigravity after connecting.

### Does the agy CLI work too?

Yes. agy follows the app’s gateway, or runs on its own row through the Gemini API, with an agy shell function so the command just works.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Cursor Private Inference on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference) and [Snow CLI on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/snow-cli). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/snow-cli

# Snow CLI on any model

Snow CLI (`snow`, the npm package `snow-ai`) keeps each API setup as a profile. magpie adds one of its own that points Snow at magpie’s gateway, so Snow can run on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

Snow keeps its settings in `~/.snow` (or `$SNOW_CONFIG_DIR`). Each profile is a file in `profiles/`, `active-profile.json` names the one in use, and `config.json` is a copy of it. magpie writes `profiles/magpie.json`: a copy of the profile you were on, with magpie’s gateway as its base URL, a key that names Snow, Chat Completions as its protocol and the model you pick as its model. It makes that profile the active one and copies it to `config.json`, as Snow’s own profile switch does. The gateway then sends each request to the model’s provider.

## Connect Snow

1. **Add providers in magpie.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Snow CLI’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under magpie.
3. **Restart open snow sessions.** Snow reads its profile at start-up.

```
magpie snow deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # Snow on DeepSeek
magpie snow default                     # back to your own profile
```

It works the same for Snow in a WSL distro on Windows: the profile there names the gateway as the distro reaches it.

## Your profiles

Your own profiles are not changed. magpie’s copies your other settings from the one you were on, but leaves out a subscription sign-in of yours (`snowcfg.oauth`). A profile of your own that happens to be named `magpie` is kept and put back. On the row, the models of your own profiles are listed too: picking one makes Snow switch to that profile.

## Windows and images

magpie sets `maxContextTokens`, `maxTokens` and `supportsVision` from its catalog for the model you pick, so Snow knows its real window and whether it takes images. A model magpie knows no limits for gets Snow’s own defaults, 200K and 64K. If you change one of these in Snow’s settings, it stays as you set it. A vision model of your own is kept only with an endpoint and key of its own. Images for a model that can’t see go through magpie’s Vision, which describes them at the gateway.

## The light model

Snow asks a light model (`basicModel`) for summaries, compaction and file search. On magpie’s profile it follows the main model, unless you pick another magpie model in the row’s small field. That pick stays when you change the main model.

## Thinking

The row’s thinking field sets `chatThinking` on magpie’s profile: a level sends `reasoning_effort` with each request, and off is Snow’s default. Only models that list reasoning levels offer it.

## Snow App

Snow App keeps API setups of its own. Its Sync Snow CLI API config button copies Snow CLI’s profiles into it, magpie’s among them, so the app can use magpie’s models too.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own models on the row, run `magpie snow default`, or take the row off magpie. Snow goes back to the profile you were on, `profiles/magpie.json` is removed, and `config.json` is a copy of your profile again.

## FAQ

### Can Snow CLI use DeepSeek, GLM or Qwen?

Yes. Any model you have in magpie can be Snow’s model: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Does magpie change my own Snow profiles?

No. It adds a profile of its own, profiles/magpie.json, and makes it the active one. Switching back makes your profile active again.

### Why does Snow show the wrong context size?

magpie sets maxContextTokens and maxTokens from its catalog for the model you pick. A value you changed in Snow yourself stays as you set it.

### Which protocol does Snow use with magpie?

Chat Completions (requestMethod chat). The row warns when magpie’s profile is set to another one.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Cursor Private Inference on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference), [Antigravity on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/antigravity) and [JetBrains Air on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/jetbrains-air). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/jetbrains-air

# JetBrains Air on any model

JetBrains Air runs its own agents (Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, Junie) on accounts signed in under its settings, with no base URL to point elsewhere. It also takes any agent that speaks the Agent Client Protocol. magpie adds one, named Magpie, so Air can run on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

Air lists custom ACP agents from `acp.json` in its config folder: `~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/Air` on macOS, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/JetBrains/Air` on Linux, `%APPDATA%\JetBrains\Air` on Windows. magpie adds an entry named `Magpie` there that starts `opencode acp`, OpenCode’s ACP server, with `OPENCODE_CONFIG` set to `magpie-opencode.json`, a file magpie keeps beside `acp.json`. That file holds magpie’s provider, its models, the model a task starts on, and `enabled_providers` narrowed to magpie. OpenCode merges it over your own config and leaves your plugins, agents and MCP servers as they are. Air’s own agents, and the accounts they run on, aren’t touched.

## Connect Air

1. **Add providers in magpie.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on JetBrains Air’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under magpie.
3. **Start a new task in Air.** Pick Magpie in its agent menu. magpie’s models and routing groups are in its model menu.

```
magpie air deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro        # the Air app
magpie air-ide deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # Air in JetBrains IDEs
```

## OpenCode

The Magpie agent is OpenCode, so OpenCode has to be installed. magpie gives Air its full path, since an app may not have your shell’s PATH: the one on PATH, else `~/.opencode/bin`, else one a JetBrains IDE or Zed installed from the ACP registry. If none is found, the row says to install it:

```
npm i -g --allow-scripts=@opencode/cli @opencode/cli
```

## The model menu

Air’s model menu for the Magpie agent is the list OpenCode reports, which is magpie’s models and routing groups and nothing of OpenCode’s own. The model picked on the row is the one a new task starts on, and also OpenCode’s small model for titles and summaries. You can pick another in Air’s menu for each task.

## Air in JetBrains IDEs

Air is also a plugin in JetBrains IDEs: bundled with 2026.3, and installed from JetBrains Marketplace in 2026.2. The plugin reads custom agents from `~/.jetbrains/acp.json` on every system, so it has a row of its own, Air (JetBrains IDEs), which adds the same Magpie agent there. Restart the IDE if Magpie isn’t listed yet. In the IDE, Air’s own Codex and Claude Agent, on their own login, run this computer’s `codex` and `claude`, so they are on magpie too while Codex and Claude Code are connected in magpie. The model on Air’s row is the Magpie agent’s alone.

## WSL projects

An IDE on Windows starts the agent of a project that lives in a WSL distro inside that distro, and refuses a Windows command there. So each running distro with OpenCode gets an entry of its own, such as `Magpie (WSL Ubuntu)`, with OpenCode’s path in the distro and a config that names the gateway as the distro reaches it.

## Provider keys in the environment

One gap is OpenCode’s: when a provider’s key is set in the environment Air starts it with (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and so on, not empty), its ACP server lists that provider and none from its config, so magpie’s models don’t show. Unset the variable, or keep the key in OpenCode’s `auth.json` instead.

## Switch back

Take the row off magpie. magpie removes the Magpie entry from `acp.json` and deletes `magpie-opencode.json`. Air’s own agents were never changed. If the Magpie entry is removed by hand, the row says Air no longer reaches magpie.

## FAQ

### Can JetBrains Air use DeepSeek, GLM or Qwen?

Yes. Pick the Magpie agent in a new Air task, and every model you have in magpie is in its model menu: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Does magpie change Air’s own agents or accounts?

No. It adds one ACP agent, Magpie, to acp.json. Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie keep their own accounts.

### Why doesn’t the Magpie agent show magpie’s models?

Usually a provider key such as OPENAI_API_KEY is set in the environment Air starts with. OpenCode then lists only that provider. Unset it, or keep the key in OpenCode’s auth.json.

### Does it work in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and other JetBrains IDEs?

Yes, through the Air plugin (bundled with 2026.3, from Marketplace in 2026.2). Connect the Air (JetBrains IDEs) row and restart the IDE.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Antigravity on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/antigravity), [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codebuddy) and [Snow CLI on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/snow-cli). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codebuddy

# CodeBuddy on any model

CodeBuddy is Tencent's AI coding tool: the CodeBuddy Code CLI (`codebuddy`, `cbc`) and the CodeBuddy IDE. Both the international edition (codebuddy.ai) and the China one (codebuddy.cn) take custom models. magpie writes your magpie models into that list, so CodeBuddy runs on DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, and those models need no CodeBuddy sign-in.

CodeBuddy Code is one npm package, `@tencent-ai/codebuddy-code`, for both editions; the China one is told apart by `CODEBUDDY_INTERNET_ENVIRONMENT=internal`. Both read custom models from `~/.codebuddy/models.json` (or `$CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR`), and the CodeBuddy IDE reads the same file. So magpie has one row, CodeBuddy, for the CLI and the IDE.

## Set up CodeBuddy

1. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on CodeBuddy's row.** On the Agents page, pick a model under magpie. magpie writes every model into models.json and the one you picked into settings.json's `model`.
3. **Start a new session.** CodeBuddy Code reads its model when a session starts: restart `codebuddy`, or run `/clear` in an open session.

```
magpie codebuddy deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
magpie codebuddy            # show what it is set to
```

## models.json

Each model magpie writes points at the magpie gateway on this computer and is asked under a Bearer key magpie gives CodeBuddy. CodeBuddy calls that address itself, not through Tencent's servers, with no CodeBuddy sign-in.

```
{"models": [{
  "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Pro", "vendor": "magpie",
  "apiKey": "…", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/chat/completions",
  "maxInputTokens": …, "maxOutputTokens": …,
  "supportsToolCall": true, "supportsImages": …, "reasoning": {…}
}, …]}
```

`maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` come from magpie's catalog; without `maxOutputTokens` CodeBuddy caps every reply at its own default. A model that thinks carries its levels (`supportedEfforts`, `defaultEffort`) and `canDisableThinking` when thinking can be turned off; a model with a window over 200K offers two sizes in `contextWindow`. CodeBuddy picks up a change to the file without a restart.

## CodeBuddy Code

In the CLI, the model a session starts on is `settings.json`'s `model`: one of magpie's ids from models.json, or one of CodeBuddy's own. magpie tells CodeBuddy's requests apart by their key, so Usage counts them under CodeBuddy.

## CodeBuddy IDE

CodeBuddy.app (codebuddy.ai) and CodeBuddy CN.app (codebuddy.cn) read the same `~/.codebuddy/models.json`. They watch the file, sync their model list when it changes, and list magpie's models in the IDE's own model picker. The IDE needs no CLI; with only the IDE installed, magpie still shows the CodeBuddy row. Two differences: the IDE always reads `.codebuddy` in your home folder, whatever `CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR` says, and it doesn't read settings.json's `model`, so the model is picked in the IDE.

## Your own models

Models you added to models.json yourself stay as they are; magpie updates only its own, in the place they were. A magpie model you turned off in CodeBuddy stays off, and a default thinking level you set on one stays while the model still offers it. When the file has `availableModels` (the models to show), magpie's are added to it and the rest you listed stay.

## WSL

On Windows, a WSL distro with CodeBuddy Code installed has its own row. It writes the distro's `~/.codebuddy/models.json`, naming the gateway as the distro reaches it, with the key it takes from there. `CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR` isn't read there.

## Switching back

Pick one of CodeBuddy's own models on the row: magpie takes its models out of models.json and sets settings.json's `model` to yours. Or from a terminal:

```
magpie codebuddy default
```

## FAQ

### Can CodeBuddy use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie writes them as custom models into ~/.codebuddy/models.json, and they show in both CodeBuddy Code's and the CodeBuddy IDE's model list.

### Do magpie's models need a CodeBuddy sign-in?

No. They call the magpie gateway on this computer under the key magpie gives CodeBuddy, not through a CodeBuddy account.

### Does the China edition and CodeBuddy CN work?

Yes. Both CLI editions are one npm package, and CodeBuddy.app and CodeBuddy CN.app read the same models.json, so one row covers them all.

### I changed the model and nothing happened.

CodeBuddy Code reads its model when a session starts. Restart codebuddy or run /clear. In the IDE, pick the model in its model picker.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Kimi Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/kimi-code), [Qwen Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwen-code) and [T3 Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/t3-code). Tencent Cloud's models: [Tencent Cloud](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/tencent-cloud). Notes on the same models: [Obsidian on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/obsidian). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/obsidian

# Obsidian on any model

Obsidian has no AI of its own; its community plugins bring it. magpie wires Copilot for Obsidian (logancyang/obsidian-copilot), which takes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you name. magpie adds a provider called magpie in every vault that has Copilot, so Obsidian's AI chat runs on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up Obsidian

1. **Install Copilot in Obsidian.** Install and turn on Copilot from Obsidian's Settings › Community plugins. magpie shows the Obsidian row once a vault has Copilot.
2. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick magpie on Obsidian's row.** On the Agents page, pick magpie. Then reload Copilot in Obsidian, and magpie's models are in its model menu.

```
magpie obsidian provider magpie
```

## Vaults

Obsidian lists its vaults in `obsidian.json` in its config folder: `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian` on a Mac, `%APPDATA%\obsidian` on Windows, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/obsidian` on Linux, or the Flatpak's and the Snap's own folders. Copilot keeps its settings in each vault's `.obsidian/plugins/copilot/data.json`. magpie wires every vault that has Copilot; after that it keeps the wired vaults up to date and wires none you haven't asked for.

## The model list

This is what magpie writes into data.json. Only these keys change; everything else in the file stays as written:

```
"providers": {"magpie": {
  "providerType": "openai-compatible", "displayName": "magpie",
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/agent/obsidian/v1",
  "requiresApiKey": false, …}},
"configuredModels": [{"providerId": "magpie", "info": {"id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", …}}, …],
"backends": {"chat": {"enabledModels": […]}},
"defaultModelKey": "…"
```

Each model carries its context size, output limit, images and thinking levels from magpie's catalog. A model new in magpie comes on in chat; a magpie model you turned off in Copilot stays off; one gone from magpie leaves every backend. Models and providers you added in Copilot yourself are untouched. The first time, Copilot's default model becomes magpie's first, and the one it had is kept to put back when you switch back.

## No key to enter

Copilot keeps API keys in Obsidian's keychain, which magpie doesn't write. So magpie's provider needs no key (`requiresApiKey: false`): its requests carry no Authorization, and the gateway takes a call with no key from this computer. Copilot calls it with fetch from Obsidian's window, so replies stream, and the gateway answers that window's CORS. The `/agent/obsidian` in the address is how magpie knows it is Obsidian, since the window's User-Agent is a browser's.

## Reloading Copilot

While Obsidian runs, Copilot holds its settings and writes data.json whole when it saves. So after wiring, reload Copilot in Settings › Community plugins (or restart Obsidian) before changing Copilot's settings, or the old settings write over magpie's. magpie says so while Obsidian is running.

## Copilot 3

magpie writes only Copilot 4's format (`providers` and `configuredModels`). Copilot 3 kept models in `activeModels`; magpie leaves such a vault alone and names it in the error. Update Copilot to 4, which moves the settings itself when it first loads.

## Switching back

Turn the row off in magpie. magpie takes its provider, its models and their places in every backend out of each vault's data.json, and puts back the default model you had while magpie's is still the default. A provider you added by hand under the name magpie, at an address that isn't magpie's Obsidian route, is yours and stays.

```
magpie obsidian default
```

## FAQ

### Can Obsidian use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes, through the Copilot for Obsidian plugin. magpie adds a magpie provider in every vault with Copilot, and every model you have in magpie is in Copilot's model menu.

### Do I enter an API key in Copilot?

No. magpie's provider needs no key: requests go to the magpie gateway on this computer, which calls the model with your key or subscription.

### Why doesn't Copilot show magpie's models?

Reload Copilot in Obsidian's Settings › Community plugins, or restart Obsidian. A vault on Copilot 3 needs Copilot 4 first.

### Does Smart Connections work?

No. Its free plugin embeds with a local model only; its API providers are in the closed Pro plugin, with keys in the keychain magpie can't write.

More apps on the same models: [Raycast](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/raycast), [Cherry Studio](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cherry-studio) and [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codebuddy). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/t3-code

# T3 Code on any model

T3 Code (pingdotgg/t3code) is a GUI that drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others. Each provider it lists is an instance of a driver, and it takes instances of your own. magpie adds two: **magpie**, on Claude Code, and **magpie · Codex**, on Codex. So T3 Code's model picker lists every model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, on the harness you choose.

## Set up T3 Code

1. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick magpie on T3 Code's row.** On the Agents page, pick magpie. magpie writes both instances into T3 Code's settings.json.
3. **Pick a model in T3 Code.** T3 Code's server watches the file and reloads it on an outside edit. In the model picker, models under magpie run on Claude Code, those under magpie · Codex on Codex.

```
magpie t3code provider magpie
```

The settings file is `~/.t3/userdata/settings.json` (`$T3CODE_HOME/userdata` when set). These are the two instances magpie writes:

```
"providerInstances": {
  "magpie": {"driver": "claudeAgent", "displayName": "magpie",
    "environment": [{"name": "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "value": "http://127.0.0.1:3425", …}, …],
    "config": {"customModels": [{"slug": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": …,
      "capabilities": {"optionDescriptors": […]}}, …]}},
  "magpie-codex": {"driver": "codex", "displayName": "magpie · Codex",
    "config": {"launchArgs": […]}}
}
```

## magpie, on Claude Code

The magpie instance is a `claudeAgent` instance: T3 Code runs Claude Code through Anthropic's Agent SDK, reading your `~/.claude` settings, with the instance's environment added. magpie sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to the gateway and the token Claude Code is routed with, so its requests are Claude Code's to the gateway. Every magpie model is one of its custom models, a 1M one marked `[1m]` as magpie marks it for Claude Code. A binary path or Claude home you gave T3's own Claude is carried over, so it runs the same Claude Code.

## magpie · Codex, on Codex

T3 Code runs each thread on the harness of the instance its model is picked from, so with the Claude Code instance alone every magpie model ran there. So magpie adds a `codex` instance, magpie · Codex. Its `launchArgs`, which T3 passes to `codex app-server` and `codex exec`, are Codex's own `-c` overrides: magpie as its model provider, and `magpie-codex-models.json` beside settings.json as its catalog, so T3 lists every magpie model under it from Codex's model list. Your `~/.codex/config.toml` isn't written, and T3's own Codex stays as it is. If you remove the instance in T3, a sync doesn't bring it back; turning T3 Code's row on again in magpie does.

## Reasoning

Without capabilities, T3 Code shows no picks beside a custom model and sends no effort. So each of magpie's custom models gets a Reasoning pick of the Claude Code levels it takes, medium first (else the lowest), which T3 hands to Claude Code as it is. A model that thinks also gets a Thinking switch, on at first; T3 sets Claude Code's `alwaysThinkingEnabled` by it, and with it off requests ask for no thinking.

## Your own settings

The instances' names, whether they are on, and every key magpie doesn't write (such as `autoCompactWindow` and `accentColor`) are yours, and what you change in T3 Code stays. Environment variables you add on magpie's instance stay too. Your own instances, their custom models and T3's other settings are untouched. magpie's are only the custom models, the gateway's variables, and the Codex instance's launch arguments and catalog.

## Claude Code's own routing

The `env` in `~/.claude/settings.json` is applied over the process', so a Claude Code routed elsewhere in its own settings takes the magpie instance's requests there; one routed through magpie or not routed at all asks the gateway. A provider switch on there, such as `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, takes it to that cloud, and magpie's check says so.

## Switching back

Turn the row off in magpie. magpie takes out only its two instances; your others and your settings stay.

```
magpie t3code default
```

## FAQ

### Can T3 Code use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie adds two provider instances to T3 Code's settings.json, and every model you have in magpie is in T3's model picker, on Claude Code or on Codex.

### What is the difference between magpie and magpie · Codex?

The same models on a different harness: those under magpie run on Claude Code, those under magpie · Codex on Codex.

### Does it change my ~/.codex/config.toml or T3's own Claude and Codex?

No. Codex's settings are launch arguments of the magpie · Codex instance alone; T3's own instances and yours stay as they are.

### Why don't requests go through magpie?

Check the env in ~/.claude/settings.json: a Claude Code routed elsewhere there, or with a cloud switch such as Bedrock on, takes the magpie instance's requests there.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codex-models), [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codebuddy), [Craft Agents on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/craft-agents) and [Every magpie model in Paseo](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/paseo). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/craft-agents

# Craft Agents on any model

Craft Agents (lukilabs/craft-agents-oss) is an Electron app that runs Claude and Pi sessions. Its models come from connections, and a custom endpoint is one. magpie adds a connection named magpie and makes it the one new sessions start on, so Craft Agents runs on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up Craft Agents

1. **Open Craft Agents once.** Craft Agents won't load a config.json without its workspaces, so magpie never makes one. It is there once Craft Agents has run.
2. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on Craft Agents' row.** On the Agents page, pick a magpie model for Craft Agents. Craft Agents watches config.json, so a running app takes it at once, from its next new session.

```
magpie craft-agents deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## The magpie connection

Connections are in `config.json` in Craft Agents' config folder (`CRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.craft-agent`). magpie's is a `pi_compat` connection on OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions; its `models` are the models picked for Craft Agents in magpie, and `defaultModel` is the one you chose.

```
"llmConnections": [
  …,
  {"slug": "magpie", "name": "magpie", "providerType": "pi_compat",
   "authType": "none",
   "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/agent/craft-agents/v1",
   "customEndpoint": {"api": "openai-completions"},
   "models": [{"id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": …}, …],
   "defaultModel": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"}
],
"defaultLlmConnection": "magpie"
```

Craft Agents resets a `defaultModel` that isn't in `models` to the first one there, so magpie always puts the model you picked in the list. A name or other field you give the connection in Craft Agents is kept when magpie syncs it.

## No key to enter

Craft Agents keeps keys apart from config.json, sealed in `credentials.enc`, which magpie doesn't open. magpie's connection has `authType: none`, which is what Craft Agents itself saves for an endpoint on this computer with no key ("Local Model"); its Pi server then sends a placeholder key, which the gateway takes from this computer. Craft Agents sends no User-Agent of its own, so `/agent/craft-agents` in the address tells the gateway which agent is asking.

## New and open sessions

New sessions start on the connection `defaultLlmConnection` names; a workspace's own default goes over it. A session keeps the connection it started on, so start a new one after switching to magpie. magpie says so while Craft Agents is running.

## Your own connections

Your connections and every other key in config.json stay as written. Before taking over the default, magpie stashes the one you had and puts it back when it steps out, where that connection is still there (else Craft Agents picks its first). If you delete the magpie connection in Craft Agents, magpie's check says it no longer reaches magpie.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in magpie: magpie takes its connection out and puts your default back. Or pick a model of one of your own connections, and magpie makes it that connection's default model.

```
magpie craft-agents default
```

## FAQ

### Can Craft Agents use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie adds a magpie connection to Craft Agents' config.json and makes it the default for new sessions; every model you picked in magpie is in it.

### Do I enter an API key in Craft Agents?

No. magpie's connection has authType none, as Craft Agents saves an endpoint on this computer with no key, and the gateway takes requests from this computer.

### Why is a session still on my old model?

A session keeps the connection it started on. Start a new session; a workspace's own default connection goes over the global one.

### magpie says to open Craft Agents first?

Craft Agents won't load a config.json without its workspaces, so magpie never makes one. Run Craft Agents once, then set it up.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [T3 Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/t3-code) and [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/codebuddy). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openchamber

# OpenChamber on any model

OpenChamber is a desktop, web and VS Code front end for OpenCode. It runs an OpenCode of its own (the desktop app bundles OpenCode 2) on your OpenCode config. magpie sets OpenChamber's default model to one of magpie's and puts magpie's provider in the OpenCode config, so OpenChamber runs on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up OpenChamber

1. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on OpenChamber's row.** On the Agents page, pick OpenChamber's default model, and a small model if you like.
3. **Start a new session.** OpenChamber takes the new model for new sessions.

```
magpie openchamber deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro          # new sessions
magpie openchamber small deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash  # titles, commit messages
```

OpenChamber's settings are under `$OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR`, `~/.config/openchamber` by default (not moved by `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). magpie writes its profile, `preferences.json`, and the copy in `settings.json` that older builds read, where that file is:

```
// ~/.config/openchamber/preferences.json
{"version": 1, "fields": {
  "defaultModel": {"value": "magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "updatedAt": …},
  "smallModelUseDefault": {"value": false, …},
  "smallModelOverride": {"value": "magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", …}
}}
```

## Which model a session gets

OpenChamber sends each new session the model it picks, in this order: the project's `defaultModel` (settings.json's projects), the profile's `defaultModel`, the agent's own, and only then OpenCode's `model`. So setting OpenCode's model alone doesn't reach OpenChamber; magpie sets the profile's `defaultModel`. A project with a default model of its own keeps it there, and magpie names the project and its model. On a new model magpie also clears the old one's `defaultVariant`, as OpenChamber's own picker does.

## The small model

OpenChamber's small model writes session titles and commit messages. It is `smallModelOverride` once `smallModelUseDefault` is false, else OpenCode's `small_model`. Picking a small model in magpie writes those two keys; switching back takes both out and leaves it to OpenCode.

## The OpenCode config

A model in OpenChamber is OpenCode's `provider/model`, so one of magpie's needs magpie's provider in the OpenCode config: `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`. A provider of your own that already sends that model to magpie's gateway is used instead of a second list of the same models. An OpenCode 2 config is written in OpenCode 2's words. Once OpenChamber steps off magpie, magpie's provider goes too, when nothing else in the OpenCode config names one of its models. Its requests count as OpenCode's, since OpenChamber's OpenCode sends them.

## New and open sessions

OpenChamber takes the new model for new sessions; sessions already open keep theirs. magpie says so while OpenChamber is running.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in magpie: magpie takes out the profile's `defaultModel` and `defaultVariant`, and OpenChamber goes back to the OpenCode config's model.

```
magpie openchamber default
```

## FAQ

### Can OpenChamber use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie sets OpenChamber's default model to the one you pick in magpie and puts magpie's provider in the OpenCode config.

### OpenCode is on magpie already; why is OpenChamber still on my old model?

OpenChamber takes a project's and its profile's own defaultModel before OpenCode's model. Pick a model on OpenChamber's own row in magpie.

### One project is still on the old model?

That project has a default model of its own in settings.json, which goes first there. magpie names the project.

### Which model writes session titles and commit messages?

The small model: smallModelOverride once smallModelUseDefault is false, else OpenCode's small_model.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [T3 Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/t3-code) and [Craft Agents on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/craft-agents). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/nanobot

# nanobot on any model

nanobot (HKUDS/nanobot, `pip install nanobot-ai`) is a personal AI assistant that answers in chat apps, its CLI and its WebUI. Its model comes from `~/.nanobot/config.json`, where any key under `providers` that isn't one of its own is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. magpie adds a magpie provider there and sets the default model to one of magpie's, so nanobot runs on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up nanobot

1. **Run nanobot once.** `nanobot onboard` or its first run makes `~/.nanobot`.
2. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on nanobot's row.** On the Agents page, pick a magpie model for nanobot. A nanobot in WSL is set up there too.

```
pip install nanobot-ai && nanobot onboard   # nanobot makes ~/.nanobot
magpie nanobot deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## What goes in config.json

magpie adds `providers.magpie` at the gateway's `/v1`, with the gateway's key and a User-Agent of `nanobot` (the OpenAI SDK's otherwise, which tells it from no one), and sets `agents.defaults` to provider magpie, model `magpie/<model id>` and the context window magpie knows the model to take. nanobot strips the `magpie/` prefix before it sends the model.

```
// ~/.nanobot/config.json
{
  "providers": {
    …,
    "magpie": {"apiBase": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1", "apiKey": "…",
               "extraHeaders": {"User-Agent": "nanobot"}}
  },
  "agents": {"defaults": {
    "provider": "magpie",
    "model": "magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
    "contextWindowTokens": …
  }}
}
```

nanobot's pydantic models read camelCase and snake_case keys alike. magpie writes nanobot's own camelCase, and takes out a snake_case spelling of the same key, so no two settings disagree.

## modelPreset

When `agents.defaults.modelPreset` names one of `modelPresets`, it goes over both provider and model. So magpie stashes it and takes it out while magpie's model is on, and puts it back when it steps out; your `modelPresets` stay as they are.

## When it takes effect

nanobot's gateway (`nanobot gateway`, the WebUI's) watches the file and takes a change at its next reply. `nanobot agent` reads it once, so restart an open `nanobot agent` chat. magpie says so while nanobot is running.

## Your own settings

The provider, model, context window and modelPreset you had under `agents.defaults` are stashed and put back when magpie steps out. Your other providers, presets and keys stay as they are. A config.json magpie made goes again once nothing is left in it. If you delete the magpie provider in nanobot, magpie's check says it no longer reaches magpie.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in magpie: magpie takes out `providers.magpie` and puts `agents.defaults` back. Or pick a model of your own, and magpie puts things back and then sets it as the model.

```
magpie nanobot default
```

## FAQ

### Can nanobot use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie adds an OpenAI-compatible magpie provider to ~/.nanobot/config.json and sets the default model to the one you pick in magpie.

### Why is nanobot still on the old model?

nanobot's gateway and WebUI take the change at their next reply; nanobot agent reads its config once, so restart the chat.

### Do I lose my modelPreset?

No. magpie stashes agents.defaults.modelPreset and takes it out (it would go over magpie's model), and puts it back when it steps out; modelPresets stay.

### Does it work for nanobot in WSL?

Yes. magpie sets up a nanobot in a WSL distro too.

More agents on the same models: [OpenClaw on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openclaw), [Hermes Agent on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/hermes), [OpenChamber on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openchamber) and [AstrBot on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/astrbot). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/astrbot

# AstrBot on any model

AstrBot (AstrBotDevs/AstrBot) is a chatbot framework that puts a model on QQ, Telegram, Discord, Lark and other platforms. It keeps every setting in one file, `data/cmd_config.json`. magpie adds an OpenAI-compatible magpie source there, an entry for each of magpie's models, and makes the one you pick AstrBot's default chat model. So your bot runs on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, with no key typed into AstrBot's WebUI.

## Set up AstrBot

1. **Start AstrBot once.** Its first start writes `data/cmd_config.json`. It needs 4.10 or later (a config with `provider_sources`).
2. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on AstrBot's row.** On the Agents page, pick a magpie model for AstrBot.
4. **Restart AstrBot.** AstrBot reads its config at start-up only; after a restart the bot is on the new model.

```
magpie astrbot deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
# then restart AstrBot
```

magpie finds AstrBot's root in this order: `ASTRBOT_ROOT`; the desktop app's `~/.astrbot`; a folder where `astrbot init` was run, either your home, `~/astrbot` or `~/AstrBot` (where its README and a clone of its source put it). For AstrBot run anywhere else, start magpie with `ASTRBOT_ROOT` set to that folder.

## What goes in cmd_config.json

Since 4.10 AstrBot splits a chat provider into two lists: `provider_sources` holds endpoints and keys, and each entry of `provider` is one model of a source. magpie adds a source with id `magpie` (OpenAI Compatible, at the gateway's `/v1`, with a key naming AstrBot, so its requests count as AstrBot's in magpie's usage), an entry `magpie/<provider>/<model>` for each model, and sets `agent_runner.config.model.provider_id` to the one you pick (`provider_settings.default_provider_id` in a file from before agent_runner).

```
// /data/cmd_config.json
{
  "provider_sources": [
    …,
    {"id": "magpie", "provider": "openai", "type": "openai_chat_completion",
     "provider_type": "chat_completion", "enable": true,
     "key": ["…"], "api_base": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1", …}
  ],
  "provider": [
    …,
    {"id": "magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "provider_source_id": "magpie",
     "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
     "modalities": ["text", "tool_use"], "max_context_tokens": …}
  ],
  "agent_runner": {"runner_type": "local",
    "config": {"model": {"provider_id": "magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"}}}
}
```

Every model is marked `tool_use`: without it AstrBot drops the model's tools, and the gateway passes a tool call on whatever the model. Images are marked as magpie knows the model sees them. A context window magpie doesn't know is 0, and AstrBot looks it up itself.

## Why it needs a restart

AstrBot reads the whole file into memory at start, and its WebUI writes the whole of it back on every save. So magpie's change needs AstrBot restarted, and a WebUI save made before that restart writes over it. magpie's check notices that its source is gone and asks you to connect again.

When `agent_runner.runner_type` isn't `local` (an outside agent runner), AstrBot doesn't ask its chat model, and magpie's check says so.

## Your own settings

Before it first writes the file, magpie copies it to `cmd_config.json.before-magpie`. Your own sources and models stay byte for byte, and so do changes you make to magpie's entries in the WebUI (a source's timeout or proxy, a model switched off, its extra body). A model picked for one chat with `/provider` lives in AstrBot's own database; it is yours and stands. AstrBot writes the file with a UTF-8 BOM, which magpie keeps.

## AstrBot in Docker

AstrBot in Docker isn't one magpie wires: its data folder is a volume magpie can't know, and the gateway on this machine's loopback isn't the container's.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in magpie: magpie takes its source and models out and puts the default chat model back to the one AstrBot was on, unless you have picked another in AstrBot since, which stands. Or pick a model of your own; magpie's models stay in the list beside it until you disconnect. Restart AstrBot after either.

```
magpie astrbot default
# then restart AstrBot
```

## FAQ

### Can AstrBot use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie adds an OpenAI-compatible magpie source to cmd_config.json, an entry for each of magpie's models, and sets the one you pick as the default chat model. Restart AstrBot to use it.

### Why is my bot still on the old model?

AstrBot reads cmd_config.json at start-up only, so restart it. Don't save anything in the WebUI before that, or it writes over magpie's change.

### magpie's source is gone. What now?

A WebUI save most likely wrote the whole file back. Connect AstrBot again in magpie, then restart AstrBot.

### Does it work for AstrBot in Docker?

Not on its own: magpie can't know the container's data volume, and this machine's loopback isn't the container's.

More agents on the same models: [nanobot on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/nanobot), [QwenPaw on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwenpaw), [OpenClaw on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openclaw) and [Every model in Cherry Studio, through magpie](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cherry-studio). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/aionui

# AionUi on any model

AionUi is an Electron desktop app that runs Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, and has a chat of its own. It keeps its model providers in its own database, their keys encrypted, so magpie writes nothing there. It opens AionUi's own add-provider link instead, which brings up AionUi's add-model form with magpie filled in, for you to confirm in AionUi. AionUi then has every model in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, and the Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot subscription you signed in to.

## Add magpie to AionUi

1. **Open AionUi once.** Once AionUi has run, its data folder has an `aionui` folder and magpie's Agents page lists it.
2. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Click Add magpie.** On AionUi's row, click Add magpie. AionUi opens Settings → Model's add form with magpie filled in: name magpie, platform custom (OpenAI-compatible), the gateway's address and a key.
4. **Confirm it in AionUi.** Nothing is added until you do.

The link magpie opens looks like this:

```
aionui://add-provider?api_key=…&base_url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A3425%2Fv1&name=magpie&platform=custom
```

If nothing opens, nothing on this computer handles AionUi's links yet: open AionUi once or install it again, then click Add magpie again.

## Picking models

The magpie provider's address ends in `/v1`, as AionUi's own OpenAI preset does, and it lists every model in magpie from the gateway, named provider/model (for example `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`). A provider you add to magpie later shows up when AionUi fetches the list again, with nothing changed in AionUi. Several accounts behind one model, the rest after a 429 and fallback work as they do for every other agent.

## From the command line

```
magpie aionui add      # opens AionUi to add magpie; confirm it there
```

## How magpie knows it was added

magpie reads AionUi's database (`aionui/aionui-backend.db` in AionUi's data folder: `~/Library/Application Support/AionUi` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\AionUi` on Windows, `~/.config/AionUi` on Linux) read-only, for a provider at the gateway's address. It can read it while AionUi runs, and never writes it. Once there is one, the row says it's added, and you can click again to add it again. When the database can't be read, magpie says it doesn't know, not that it isn't added.

## Usage and keys

The key in the link is AionUi's own, so its requests are counted as AionUi's in magpie's usage, apart from other agents.

## FAQ

### Do I need an API key to use Claude or ChatGPT in AionUi?

No. Sign in to a Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot subscription in magpie and its models show up under AionUi's magpie provider.

### Does magpie change AionUi's settings?

No. magpie opens AionUi's own add-model form, and you confirm it. It only reads AionUi's database to show whether magpie was added.

### What address and platform does the magpie provider use?

Platform custom (OpenAI-compatible), at http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1, or the gateway address you set in magpie.

### AionUi isn't on magpie's Agents page.

magpie lists AionUi once it has run on this computer. Open AionUi once, then look again.

More desktop apps on the same models: [Every model in Cherry Studio, through magpie](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cherry-studio) and [AstrBot on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/astrbot). Using coding agents too? See [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/subscriptions). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/qwenpaw

# QwenPaw on any model

QwenPaw (agentscope-ai/QwenPaw, formerly CoPaw) is a personal assistant app with agents of its own. magpie adds an OpenAI-compatible magpie provider to QwenPaw with every model in magpie listed, and sets the model you pick as an agent's `active_model`. So QwenPaw's agents run on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, a different one for each agent if you like.

## Set up QwenPaw

1. **Start QwenPaw once.** Run `qwenpaw app` so it writes its agents' settings (`agent.json`).
2. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on QwenPaw's row.** On the Agents page, pick a magpie model for QwenPaw, and an effort if you want one.
4. **Restart QwenPaw after the first connect.** QwenPaw reads its provider files at start-up only; after one restart it is on magpie.

```
magpie qwenpaw deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro          # the default agent
magpie qwenpaw#writer deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash  # the agent named writer
magpie qwenpaw effort high                        # thinking_level
```

## What magpie writes

QwenPaw's working folder is `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR`; without it, a legacy `~/.copaw` when there is one, else `~/.qwenpaw`. Its secret folder is `QWENPAW_SECRET_DIR` (which the working folder's `.env` may set too), else `<working folder>.secret`, such as `~/.qwenpaw.secret`.

magpie writes `<secret folder>/providers/custom/magpie.json`, the way QwenPaw's console saves a provider from Add provider: OpenAI Chat Completions (`OpenAIChatModel`) at the gateway's `/v1`, a key naming QwenPaw, and each of magpie's models in `extra_models`. It then sets `active_model` in the agent's `agent.json` to provider magpie and the model you pick; the effort goes in `thinking_level` (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or empty for inherit, the model's own).

```
// ~/.qwenpaw.secret/providers/custom/magpie.json
{"id": "magpie", "name": "magpie", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
 "api_key": "…", "chat_model": "OpenAIChatModel", "is_custom": true,
 "extra_models": [{"id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", …}, …]}

// ~/.qwenpaw/workspaces/default/agent.json
{"active_model": {"provider_id": "magpie", "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"},
 "thinking_level": "high", …}
```

QwenPaw keeps keys encrypted (starting `ENC:`). magpie writes the key in plain text and QwenPaw encrypts it at its next start, which is how its own files hold a key, so the key goes nowhere QwenPaw doesn't keep it. The provider file is readable by you alone (0600).

## When it takes effect

QwenPaw reads its provider files once, at start, so restart it after the first connect and after magpie's models change; until then a turn on magpie's model fails with `Provider 'magpie' not found`. A model picked for an agent after that needs no restart: QwenPaw reads `agent.json` again when it changes and asks for the model on every turn, so the new one is used from the next message.

## Several agents

Each of QwenPaw's agents is a row in magpie: `qwenpaw` is the default agent, which is always there, and any other is `qwenpaw#<id>`. Only an agent on QwenPaw's own backend (qwenpaw, the default) runs that model; one on an ACP backend runs another program, so magpie doesn't wire it and asks you to switch it to QwenPaw's own backend first.

## Your own settings

The agent's `active_model` from before is stashed and put back when magpie steps out. `fallback_models` and `subagent_model` are left alone. What you change in magpie's provider in QwenPaw's console (a model's window, its generation settings, the provider's headers) stays. If you switch magpie's provider off or delete it in QwenPaw, magpie's check says it no longer reaches magpie.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in magpie: magpie puts the agent's `active_model` back. It removes `custom/magpie.json` only once no agent names magpie's provider any more, in a fallback or subagent model either. Or pick a model of one of your own providers; magpie's provider stays in the list until you disconnect.

```
magpie qwenpaw default
```

## FAQ

### Can QwenPaw use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie writes an OpenAI-compatible magpie provider into QwenPaw's secret folder and sets the model you pick as the agent's active_model. Restart QwenPaw once after the first connect.

### Why does it say Provider 'magpie' not found?

QwenPaw reads its provider files at start-up only. Restart QwenPaw once after connecting; after that a new model is used from the next message, with no restart.

### Does it work for CoPaw?

Yes. QwenPaw was CoPaw; with a legacy ~/.copaw there, magpie uses it as the working folder, as QwenPaw does.

### Can each agent use a different model?

Yes. The default agent is the qwenpaw row in magpie and any other is qwenpaw#, each with its own model and effort.

More agents on the same models: [AstrBot on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/astrbot), [nanobot on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/nanobot) and [OpenClaw on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/openclaw). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/zoo-code

# Zoo Code on any model

Zoo Code (Zoo-Code-Org/Zoo-Code, the VS Code extension ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code, a fork of Roo Code) keeps its provider profiles in VS Code's secret storage, encrypted and out of reach. But on every start it imports the file its `zoo-code.autoImportSettingsPath` setting names, as its own Settings → Import does. magpie writes that file: one OpenAI-compatible profile named magpie, at the local gateway, on the model you pick. So Zoo Code runs on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up Zoo Code

1. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Zoo Code's row.** With the Zoo Code extension installed, magpie's Agents page has a Zoo Code row; pick a model.
3. **Reload the VS Code window.** Run **Developer: Reload Window** from the Command Palette; Zoo Code imports magpie's profile as it starts and switches to it.

```
magpie zoo-code deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
# VS Code: Developer: Reload Window
```

## What magpie writes

magpie writes the file to import in Zoo Code's own folder in VS Code's User folder, `globalStorage/zoocodeorganization.zoo-code/settings/magpie-import.json`, beside the settings files Zoo Code keeps itself. It then points `zoo-code.autoImportSettingsPath` at it in VS Code's `settings.json`. A value of your own is kept aside and put back on Disconnect.

```
// /globalStorage/zoocodeorganization.zoo-code/settings/magpie-import.json
{"providerProfiles": {"currentApiConfigName": "magpie",
  "apiConfigs": {"magpie": {"id": "magpie", "apiProvider": "openai",
    "openAiBaseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1", "openAiApiKey": "…",
    "openAiModelId": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "openAiStreamingEnabled": true,
    "openAiCustomModelInfo": {"contextWindow": …, "maxTokens": …, "supportsImages": …}}}}}

// /settings.json
"zoo-code.autoImportSettingsPath": "…/magpie-import.json"
```

The profile uses Zoo Code's OpenAI Compatible provider on the gateway's Chat Completions (`/v1`), with a key naming Zoo Code; its requests say `ZooCode/<version>` as their User-Agent, so magpie's usage counts them under Zoo Code. `openAiCustomModelInfo` carries the model's window (Zoo Code trims a conversation to it; 128K when it isn't told), what a reply may take, and whether it sends images. Imported profiles are merged over yours, which stay.

## When it takes effect

Zoo Code reads the file only when it starts, so reload the window once after you pick. While connected it imports the file again on every start, so each start puts it back on magpie's profile; a profile you switch to inside Zoo Code meanwhile is one magpie can't see, and the next start comes back. When magpie's models or the key change, magpie updates the file, used from the next start.

## VS Code profiles

VS Code's default profile and each profile you made has its own `settings.json`; magpie points the setting at its file in every one, and in a profile made later too. If any of them can't be written, all are put back as they were.

## Zoo Code for JetBrains

Zoo Code for JetBrains runs the same extension in its own extension host, which is handed an empty configuration on every start, so the setting can't reach it; and it keeps its secrets in `~/.zoo-code/secrets.json`, a store of its own with no lock and no documented format. magpie writes neither, so the JetBrains build isn't wired.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in magpie: magpie puts the setting back in every `settings.json` and removes the import file. A profile once imported lives in Zoo Code's secret storage, which magpie can't write, so the magpie profile stays in Zoo Code's list; switch from it or delete it in Zoo Code.

```
magpie zoo-code default
```

## FAQ

### Can Zoo Code use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie writes a magpie profile Zoo Code imports when it starts, on the local gateway's Chat Completions and the model you pick in magpie. Reload the window once after you pick.

### Why didn't Zoo Code change after I picked a model?

Zoo Code imports profiles only when it starts. Run Developer: Reload Window from VS Code's Command Palette.

### Does it work in Zoo Code for JetBrains?

No. The JetBrains build is handed an empty configuration on every start, so the import setting can't reach it, and its secrets file has no documented format; magpie writes neither.

### Why is the magpie profile still there after Disconnect?

An imported profile lives in Zoo Code's encrypted secret storage, which magpie can't write. magpie stops the import and puts the setting back; the profile is yours to switch from or delete in Zoo Code.

More agents on the same models: [Cline on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/cline), [Goose on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/goose) and [Hermes Agent on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/hermes). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/jcode

# jcode on any model

jcode (1jehuang/jcode) is a coding agent in Rust that keeps its settings in `config.toml`. A provider of your own is a named profile, `[providers.<name>]`, as `jcode provider add` writes it. magpie adds itself as the profile magpie, at the local gateway, with every magpie model listed, and starts jcode on the model you pick. So jcode runs on any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up jcode

1. **Add a provider in magpie.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on jcode's row.** With jcode installed, magpie's Agents page has a jcode row; pick a model.
3. **Start jcode.** A new jcode starts on that model; restart a session that is already open.

```
magpie jcode deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
jcode   # /model lists every magpie model, /effort its levels
```

## What magpie writes

jcode's folder is `$JCODE_HOME`, else `~/.jcode`. In its `config.toml` magpie writes `[providers.magpie]`: `type = "openai-compatible"` (jcode's Chat Completions client), `base_url` at the gateway's `/v1`, an `api_key` naming jcode, and `requires_api_key = true`. That last one is there because jcode takes a gateway on loopback as needing no key and then sends none, and the key is how the gateway knows the request is jcode's. It then sets `default_provider` and `default_model` in `[provider]` to magpie and the model you pick.

```
# ~/.jcode/config.toml
[provider]
default_provider = "magpie"
default_model = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"

[providers.magpie]
type = "openai-compatible"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
api_key = "…"
requires_api_key = true
models = [
  { id = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", context_window = …, input = ["text"], reasoning = true },
  …
]
```

## /model and /effort

Each of magpie's models is an entry in `models`, so jcode's `/model` picker lists them all and switches between them. Each entry carries the context window (128K when magpie doesn't know it; jcode would take 200K) and whether it takes images; a model with effort levels gets `reasoning = true`, so jcode's `/effort` offers them. A `reasoning_effort` you set on one of magpie's models stays while the model has that level. When magpie's models change, magpie updates the list.

## When it takes effect

jcode reads its settings at start-up, so restart an open jcode session to use a new model or list; magpie says so while jcode is running.

## Your own settings

The profile and model `[provider]` named before are stashed and put back when magpie steps out. Every other key of the file is yours and stays as written, your own keys in magpie's profile too (headers, extra_body, a model's reasoning_effort). A `config.toml` that doesn't parse is an error and left as it is, never taken as empty. When jcode saves its settings itself it writes the models as `[[providers.magpie.models]]` tables; magpie folds them back into one array on its next write.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in magpie: when jcode still starts on magpie, magpie puts `[provider]` back as it was; a pick you made in jcode since is yours and stands. Then the whole `[providers.magpie]` goes, with your own keys in it. Or pick one of jcode's own models, and magpie sets `default_model` to it.

```
magpie jcode default
```

## FAQ

### Can jcode use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. magpie writes an openai-compatible [providers.magpie] profile into jcode's config.toml at the local gateway, and starts jcode on the model you pick.

### Can I switch magpie's models in jcode's /model?

Yes. Every magpie model is in the magpie profile's models, so /model lists and switches them; a model with effort levels offers them in /effort.

### Why didn't jcode change after I picked a model?

jcode reads its settings at start-up. Restart the open jcode session.

### Do my settings stay after switching back?

Yes. magpie removes only [providers.magpie], and puts [provider] back when jcode still starts on magpie; every other key stays as written.

More agents on the same models: [Crush on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/crush), [Models in OpenCode](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Goose on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/goose) and [Reasonix Studio on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/reasonix). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/paseo

# Every magpie model in Paseo

Paseo (getpaseo/paseo) is an app that runs Claude Code, Codex and others for you. It starts the same Claude Code, so a Claude Code connected to magpie goes through magpie in Paseo too. But Paseo lists models itself, and most of the models magpie serves aren't in its picker. magpie writes them into Paseo's own `additionalModels`, so Paseo's Claude model picker offers every model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Paseo

1. **Connect Claude Code to magpie first.** On magpie's Agents page, pick a magpie model for Claude Code. The ids Paseo lists are served by a Claude Code that is on magpie.
2. **Switch Paseo's row on.** With a `~/.paseo` folder, magpie has a Paseo row. Pick magpie: every magpie model in Paseo's Claude model picker.
3. **Restart Paseo's daemon.** Paseo reads its model list when its daemon starts; after a restart magpie's models are there.

```
magpie claude deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro   # Claude Code on magpie first
magpie paseo magpie                      # every magpie model in Paseo's picker
```

## Why Paseo needs its own switch

Claude Code's own `/model` reads modelPicker in `~/.claude/settings.json`, where magpie writes every model when it connects Claude Code. Paseo never reads modelPicker: its list is its own first-party models plus settings.json's `model` and a few `ANTHROPIC_*_MODEL` tier variables. So with only Claude Code connected, magpie's models other than the main one and the tiers aren't in Paseo's picker. Paseo also appends `agents.providers.claude.additionalModels` from its own config, each id passed to Claude Code as written, and that is where magpie writes.

## What magpie writes

Paseo's folder is `PASEO_HOME`, else `~/.paseo`. In `config.json` magpie adds one `{id, label, description}` entry per model to `agents.providers.claude.additionalModels`: the same ids, [1m] marks and names as Claude Code's `/model`, with a description ending `via magpie`, which is how magpie knows its own entries.

```
// ~/.paseo/config.json
{"agents": {"providers": {"claude": {"additionalModels": [
  {"id": "my-own-model", "label": "…", "description": "…"},
  {"id": "…", "label": "…", "description": "via magpie"},
  {"id": "…", "label": "…", "description": "1M context · via magpie"}
]}}}}
```

Your own entries keep their place and come first. An id you listed yourself stays yours, and magpie doesn't add it again. A list magpie can't read is left as it is. When magpie's models change, magpie updates its entries.

## When it takes effect

Paseo reads its model list when its daemon starts, so restart Paseo's daemon to see magpie's models; magpie says so while Paseo is running. Claude Code itself must be connected to magpie too, for those ids to be served.

## Switching back

Set Paseo's row back to default in magpie: magpie takes out only the entries whose description ends `via magpie`, and yours stay; with none left, `additionalModels` goes.

```
magpie paseo default
```

## FAQ

### Why doesn't Paseo's model picker show magpie's models?

Paseo doesn't read Claude Code's modelPicker; it lists its own models, settings.json's model and a few ANTHROPIC_*_MODEL variables. Switch Paseo's row on in magpie and magpie writes every model into Paseo's additionalModels.

### Does Claude Code need to be connected first?

Yes. Paseo passes those ids as written to the Claude Code it starts, and magpie serves them once Claude Code is connected to magpie.

### I switched it on and still see nothing. Why?

Paseo reads its model list when its daemon starts. Restart Paseo's daemon.

### Will my own additionalModels be changed?

No. magpie adds and removes only entries whose description ends via magpie; yours come first and keep their place.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [T3 Code on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/t3-code) and [Craft Agents on any model](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/craft-agents). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF).

---

Source: https://usemagpie.ai/docs/reasonix

# Reasonix Studio on any model

Reasonix Studio 2.x and its CLI share one `config.toml` and `.env`. magpie adds a provider named magpie there, pointing at magpie's local gateway, so Reasonix's executor and planner can each be any model you have in magpie: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription. Your other providers, keys and project or session settings are left alone.

## Set up Reasonix

1. **Open magpie's Agents page.** Find the Reasonix Studio row. Its model field is called executor.
2. **Pick a magpie model.** The list has two groups: Reasonix Studio's own models and the ones via magpie. Pick one of the latter; magpie writes the provider and key, then sets `default_model` to `magpie/<model>`.
3. **Set effort and a planner if you want.** A model with effort levels can take an effort. The planner can be a different model, or off to turn the separate planner off.

```
magpie reasonix magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro   # executor
magpie reasonix effort high
magpie reasonix planner magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash # a separate planner, or: off
```

## What magpie writes

Reasonix's folder is `REASONIX_HOME`; without it, `%APPDATA%\reasonix` on Windows and `~/.reasonix` elsewhere. A Reasonix in WSL uses Linux's `~/.reasonix`, with the gateway as the distro reaches it. magpie writes:

```
# ~/.reasonix/config.toml
default_model = "magpie/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"

[[providers]]
name = "magpie"
kind = "openai"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
api_key_env = "MAGPIE_REASONIX_API_KEY"
models = ["…", "…"]
default = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
reasoning_protocol = "openai"
no_proxy = true

[providers.model_overrides."deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"]
supported_efforts = ["…"]
context_window = …
max_output_tokens = …

# ~/.reasonix/.env
MAGPIE_REASONIX_API_KEY=…
```

Each model carries its context window, max output, image support and effort levels; a model with no effort levels gets `reasoning_protocol = "none"`. When magpie's models change, magpie updates the provider. When Studio has a `[desktop] provider_access` list, magpie adds magpie to it. The key goes only in `.env`; config.toml names the variable.

magpie only touches its own entry. If there is already a magpie provider magpie didn't make, another provider uses `MAGPIE_REASONIX_API_KEY`, or `.env` sets it twice, magpie stops with an error rather than overwrite. magpie keeps a restore record in its own config folder (settings only, never an upstream credential) to put your `default_model` back when you switch back.

## Executor and planner

The executor is `default_model` and the planner is `[agent] planner_model`; each can come from magpie or from one of Reasonix's own providers. While the planner still uses magpie, magpie's provider stays, even with the executor back on your own model.

## When it takes effect

Reasonix Studio 2.x and the native 1.39.x/2.x CLI read global settings at startup, so start a new process after a change. A model set for a project or session overrides the executor and planner.

## Switching back

Switching back undoes only what magpie added: the magpie provider goes, `default_model` returns to what it was before (or goes if there was none), magpie leaves `provider_access`, and magpie's key leaves `.env`; a file magpie created is removed once empty. A model you picked later, and edits to other providers and keys, stay. You can also just pick a model from the Reasonix Studio group.

```
magpie reasonix default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in Reasonix Studio?

On magpie's Agents page, pick a via-magpie model as Reasonix Studio's executor. magpie adds a magpie provider to config.toml, the key to .env, and sets default_model to magpie/.
